title: Getting started
text:
FDUpdate

FDUpdate is a secure, product-neutral update platform for Windows and Linux.

-   FDUpdater   is a Rust service, CLI, and embeddable contract library. It
  verifies signed releases, stages and atomically activates updates, checks
  health, and rolls back safely.
-   FDUpdate Server   is a self-hosted release, enrollment, rollout, and feedback
  service built around Eclipse hawkBit. Its gateway keeps hawkBit, databases,
  signing keys, and administration private.

The protocol works with any compatible self-hosted endpoint; the client has no
vendor-controlled dependency.  update.fedrv.de  currently serves the owner's
internal installations. A managed public cloud service is not offered today.

   Use cases

FDUpdate supports standalone background updates, applications retaining their
own installer/UI, public and private repositories, scoped installation grants,
staged rollout/rollback, one-time download sharing, server self-update, and
COT service Telegram notifications for configured operators.

   Quick start

Install the pinned Rust 1.98 toolchain, then:

   text
git clone https://github.com/fedrnv/FDUpdate.git
cd FDUpdate
cargo build --workspace --all-targets --locked
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo run -p fdupdater --bin FDUpdater -- --version
   

All supported operations use CLI commands; an IDE is optional. Start with the
 integration guide  docs/software-integration.md ,  application-managed guide  docs/application-managed-updates.md ,
or  self-hosting guide  docs/self-hosting.md .

   Architecture and trust

Remote metadata never grants local paths, services, or keys. Product-scoped
Ed25519 signatures, compatibility, replay, rollout and rollback checks run before
staging. Activation preserves the prior version with deterministic recovery.
Server delivery rechecks installation identity, repository grant, scope and
rollout. See  architecture  docs/architecture.md  and  security  SECURITY.md .

title: Architecture
text:
Architecture overview

FDUpdater consumes signed product-neutral contracts. Local registration owns
paths, service control, health commands, and trusted public keys. The updater
verifies, stages, atomically activates, checks health, and preserves rollback.

FDUpdate Server exposes one TLS gateway. FDUpdate services authorize enrollment,
repositories, publication, downloads, rollout, feedback, and operator actions.
hawkBit 1.1.0 and MariaDB remain private. Signing is a short-lived process with an
isolated key. Persistent data, config, secrets, binaries, and logs are separate.

The supported topology is one Linux host and one organization. Tenant-safe
extension contracts add default-deny ownership, backend-neutral immutable objects,
metering, and quotas without billing, signup, or mandatory cloud service.

Normative decisions:  ADR-0001  ../Tasks/decisions/ADR-0001-product-neutral-update-contracts.md ,
 ADR-0002  ../Tasks/decisions/ADR-0002-product-scoped-release-trust.md ,
 ADR-0003  ../Tasks/decisions/ADR-0003-fdupdate-server-hawkbit-architecture.md , and
 ADR-0004  ../Tasks/decisions/ADR-0004-explicit-installation-repository-grants.md .

title: Client integration
text:
Integrating software with FDUpdater

FDUpdater updates an application only after a local administrator registers an exact instance, product and component. Applications keep their own UI and business logic. They implement readiness and health through the public contracts and never add product branches to FDUpdater core.

   1. Define stable target identities

Choose lowercase bounded  product_id ,  component_id  and per-install  instance_id  values. A multi-component installation uses one instance and product with separate component IDs. A single-binary product has one component. Keep executable versions separate from configuration, data, credentials, databases, workspaces and logs.

Use  fdupdater_conformance::FixtureProduct  and  validate_matrix  to validate the same identity and layout assumptions exercised by the reference products:

   rust
use fdupdater_conformance::{FixtureLayout, FixtureProduct, validate_matrix};

let products = vec! 
    FixtureProduct::new "suite-a", "product-a",  "server", "agent" , FixtureLayout::MultiComponent ?,
    FixtureProduct::new "suite-b", "product-b",  "desktop" , FixtureLayout::SingleBinary ?,
    FixtureProduct::new "suite-c", "product-c",  "relay" , FixtureLayout::SingleBinary ?,
 ;
validate_matrix &products ?;
  Ok::<  , fdupdater_conformance::ConformanceError>    
   

   2. Register only local authority

Create a  TargetReceipt  for each component. The receipt supplies the administrator-selected installation root, executable name, service binding, health policy, protected data roots and ownership identities. Release metadata cannot supply or widen any of these values. New targets default to the  release  channel; an authenticated local operator may set  prerelease  independently for an exact target.

The installation root and data directories must already exist and must not overlap FDUpdater state or another installation. Use  process  only for an explicitly supervised child process. Use the matching native service manager for production system services. A systemd or Windows service definition must execute the stable activation path  <installation_root>/<executable_name>  from its local receipt. FDUpdater atomically materializes the selected hash-verified slot at that path while the service is stopped, then starts the receipt-bound service. Service definitions, arguments and paths remain local administrator policy.

   3. Publish the signed release contract

The  unified release protocol  unified-release-protocol.md  is shared by the
standalone service, embedded clients and FDUpdate Server.

Publish canonical  fdupdate/release/v1  data inside  fdupdate/signed-release/v1 . Each artifact binds the target, platform, architecture, SemVer, HTTPS URL, size, SHA-256, compatibility, rollout, rollback and product-scoped signing key. hawkBit metadata and the standalone manifest provider carry the same signed envelope. Neither transport authorizes a release.

For private standalone delivery, use the runtime  gateway  provider together
with target enrollment. The local target's persisted  update_channel  is sent on
every check, including FDUpdater's own target, and is still enforced locally
after the signed response arrives. Approval provides identity only; the server
must separately grant the installation access to a repository. Removing either
approval or that repository grant prevents new checks, downloads and reports.

Provision public trust keys locally. The runtime never receives a signing private key. A candidate must pass manifest and artifact signatures, replay cursor, channel, platform, architecture, updater-version, installed-version, component dependency, rollout and downgrade checks before staging.

    Bootstrap each installation with its own identity

For a standalone target, set  enrollment.installation_key_file  to a protected
file containing the 64-character reusable installation key. Keep the secret out
of command arguments and ordinary configuration.  code_file  remains a mutually
exclusive compatibility name for older one-time codes. FDUpdater creates and
persists the installation's Ed25519 identity and exact signed request before the
first network attempt. An interrupted or offline attempt therefore retries the
same identity and consumes no additional server quota; deleting the protected
state creates a new identity and consumes a new slot.

The key is attached only while the local enrollment has no authenticated server
decision. After the first pending/approved/denied decision, later polling omits
the bootstrap key. Update checks, package downloads and reports use only the
installation-specific credential from the signed approval decision. A rejected
or exhausted key returns the distinct  EnrollmentError::Rejected ; unavailability
remains retryable without replacing the identity.

Embedded applications use  fdupdater_enrollment::InstallationKey  for their own
protected file, stdin, or secret-input path. Its debug representation is always
  REDACTED  . Each application instance opens  EnrollmentClient  with its own
state root and instance ID, supplies the key only on the bootstrap request, and
then passes the resulting client to  fdupdater_app_mode . Reusing one bootstrap
key does not share the local private key, instance ID, approval credential, update
state or package cache.

    Report managed FDUpdater liveness

An approved standalone FDUpdater creates  ManagedUpdaterHeartbeat  with
 EnrollmentClient::managed_updater_heartbeat . The client persists and increments
the heartbeat sequence before returning the signed document, so a restart or an
uncertain network result cannot reuse a sequence. It signs the instance ID,
updater version, send time, sequence and random nonce with the same installation
Ed25519 identity used for enrollment.

Send the document to
 POST /v1/updater/{tenant}/{product}/heartbeat  with the installation credential
as  Authorization: Bearer ...  and the exact instance ID in
 X-FDUpdate-Instance . The server requires current approval, matching scope and
identity, a valid signature, a bounded timestamp and a sequence greater than the
last durably accepted value. A duplicate or older sequence returns  409 ; invalid
credentials, signatures, scopes and revoked identities fail authorization.
Liveness is derived from the server receive time. A stale heartbeat is an
observation state and never authorizes a release or reports an update failure.

    Bind the applications managed by an updater

Approval, heartbeat and repository access do not implicitly give an FDUpdater authority over an application. Using the private operator API, bind the approved updater instance to each exact product/component, repository, platform, architecture and locally selected release channel. Grant check and update separately. Check-only bindings can report installed versions and health but receive no assignment or package.

Binding changes use an expected revision. The first bind uses revision zero; every later bind uses the revision returned by the installation inventory. Unbind disables the policy and advances its revision, so a delayed prior request cannot silently restore authority. The server rechecks the current binding and repository grant during check, package download and result reporting. Revocation, repository removal, channel change or unbind therefore takes effect without rewriting existing assignments.

   4. Implement readiness and health

An application that must quiesce implements the authenticated loopback readiness protocol. It stops accepting work, checkpoints active work, flushes durable state, releases exclusive resources and then returns  ready . It may return bounded  defer_until  or  reject ; timeout and disconnect fail closed.

title: Application-managed updates
text:
Application-managed updates

Application-managed mode lets an existing application keep its UI, installer,
restart policy and recovery behavior. FDUpdater supplies a versioned Rust
check/package/report contract through  fdupdater-app-mode ; it never receives an
application install path and writes packages only below its protected state root.

The application first creates an  ApplicationCheckRequest  with its installation
identity, target, platform, architecture, channel, updater version and installed
component versions.  ApplicationUpdateService::check  accepts remote metadata only
through the same approved enrollment gate used by ordinary updates. Its response
contains the assignment ID, display version, signed size and digest, release cursor
and the exact  SignedRelease  supplied by the assignment service. The service
verifies the release signature, artifact signature, target, compatibility, rollout
and release channel before persisting or returning that response.

 prepare_package  streams the assigned bytes into a bounded temporary file below
 application-packages , checks the signed size and SHA-256 digest, and atomically
caches the verified package.  open_package  returns a read-only  VerifiedPackage 
stream for the exact assignment after rechecking current enrollment approval and
the signed release. The host application copies that stream into its own installer
or staging flow. FDUpdater does not modify the application tree, run the installer
or restart the application in this mode.

For lightweight self-update without the FDUpdater daemon, implement
 ApplicationSelfUpdateHost . The library passes only a  PackageDescriptor  and
the already verified  VerifiedPackage  stream to the host's  stage  callback.
 stage_application_update  must leave the running installation unchanged and
returns an opaque host-owned prepared value.  activate_application_update  then
invokes the host's external restart helper and health check; restart failure,
health failure or an unhealthy result invokes  rollback_and_restart  before an
error is returned.  rollback_application_update  exposes the same exact host
rollback for an explicit user action.

The host owns installation paths, atomic replacement and durable recovery for its
opaque prepared value. A self-updating process should execute restart and recovery
from its installer or a small external helper so interruption cannot leave the
running executable half-replaced. The host must preserve the previous verified
version until health succeeds. No path, command or helper identity comes from
release metadata. A statically linked library is updated only by staging and
restarting a newly built owning application; the SDK does not hot-swap library
bytes.

After its own installation flow, the application sends an
 ApplicationReportRequest  for the same assignment. An  installed  result must name
the assigned version and requires a previously verified package.  failed  and
 deferred  results may include a bounded, non-control-character detail for the
remote service, while structured audit events contain only the assignment, target,
phase, version and outcome. An identical report is idempotent; a conflicting second
report is rejected.

Anonymous, pending, denied, revoked and wrong-target identities are rejected before
metadata or artifact transport. Approval is checked again for package access and
reporting, so later revocation also fails closed. Network retries are explicitly
bounded. Invalid signatures, expired or replayed releases, corrupt packages and
locally altered assignment metadata are rejected.

Operators can inspect the non-secret local status through the authenticated,
read-only loopback API or CLI:

   text
FDUpdater app-updates --endpoint 127.0.0.1:PORT --credential-file ABSOLUTE  --instance INSTANCE_ID 
   

The result exposes assignment ID, local target, version, phase and final outcome.
It excludes enrollment credentials, signed metadata, report detail and package
paths.

The server-facing contract fixture and denial matrix run with:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdater-app-mode
cargo test -p fdupdater-app-mode --test denied_states

title: Enrollment
text:
Installation enrollment

Each installed application instance has its own Ed25519 identity. FDUpdater generates the key inside its protected local state root, persists it with private-file permissions and sends only a signed enrollment request containing the instance ID, public key and random nonce. Reopening the same instance reuses that identity and the exact pending request; a different instance receives a different key.

The enrollment authority returns a canonical signed decision bound to the request digest, instance and public key. FDUpdater accepts strictly increasing revisions and exposes four states:  pending ,  approved ,  denied  and  revoked . A revoked identity cannot return to another state. Approval credentials remain inside the protected signed state and are never returned by status, CLI output or audit records.

Only  approved  returns a credential, and only for a target explicitly assigned in the decision. Anonymous, pending, denied, revoked and wrong-target requests fail closed before a metadata or artifact transport can be called. Authority unavailability uses a bounded retry count and retains the same signed request.

   Installation Account authorization

An installer may authorize the signed software identity with an enabled
Installation Account ID or email, its current password, and the exact non-empty
set of private repositories requested by the installed software. The request is
schema-versioned and sent to the normal product enrollment endpoint. The account
must currently grant every requested repository; the server never expands the
set from the account's other grants.

The human password exists only in zeroizing request memory and is not written to
FDUpdater state, registry state, logs, audit, or the issued installation
credential. The account is re-read and authenticated while its durable shared
lock is held through the registry decision. Registration quota is counted by
distinct signed instance identity; concurrent attempts cannot overrun it.

An identical pending identity is approved with the durable outcome
 performed_with_installation_account , retaining its earlier submission audit.
An exact retry returns the same signed decision without consuming quota. A
changed repository set, insufficient grants, wrong password, disabled account,
exhausted quota, or revoked identity fails closed. Each successful installation
receives its own credential and does not retain the Installation Account
password.

   Installation keys

An operator can issue a reusable installation key for one product/component with
an exact positive registration limit. The server persists only a domain-separated
SHA-256 verifier, a non-secret key ID, expiry and disable state, the current
repository allowlist, and a ledger of distinct installation instance IDs. The
plaintext key is returned only by the issuance response.

Each redemption still carries the installation's own signed Ed25519 enrollment
request. A retry of that exact identity is idempotent and does not consume another
slot. A different identity consumes one slot, remains  pending , and needs normal
operator approval. Once the limit is reached, concurrent new identities fail
closed. Expiry and disabling stop new identities while preserving idempotent
retries and the historical ledger; denial, revocation, or uninstall does not
refund a slot.

The operator endpoints are:

-  POST /v1/operator/installation-keys  to issue a key with
   max_installations  and  allowed_repositories ;
-  POST /v1/operator/installation-keys/list  to return verifier-free key status
  and usage counts;
-  POST /v1/operator/installation-keys/update  to change the future admission
  limit/disable state, repository allowlist, or the separate existing-update
  suspension flag.

The earlier  /v1/operator/enrollment-codes  issuance route remains compatible and
defaults omitted policy fields to a limit of one and an empty repository allowlist.
Schema 1 and 2 registry snapshots migrate consumed one-time codes to a one-entry
ledger without increasing their access.

Applications can keep their existing UI and read the state through the authenticated local API or CLI:

   text
FDUpdater enrollment --endpoint 127.0.0.1:PORT --credential-file ABSOLUTE  --instance INSTANCE_ID 
   

The result contains the instance ID, public-key fingerprint, state and decision revision. It contains no private key or approval credential. Enrollment transitions use the structured audit adapter and must be recorded before an approval is committed.

   Registration audit

The device gateway atomically persists one redacted event for each distinct
registration outcome: pending, denied, approved replay, administrator approval,
Installation Account performance, or an unavailable delegated authority. Exact
retries are idempotent. Events contain the request digest, outcome provenance,
tenant, product, components, complete repository set, optional Installation
Account ID, software instance, sequence, and server time. Passwords, installation
keys, bearer credentials, signed decisions, email addresses, and request bodies
are never stored in this audit.

The authenticated gateway query is
 POST /v1/operator/registration-audit/query . It accepts bounded time, outcome,
product/component, repository, Installation Account ID, instance, and page
filters. The caller must supply its complete repository allowlist. An event is
visible to a repository-scoped caller only when every repository on the event is
within that allowlist; a manipulated repository filter returns no rows.
Unscoped events are reserved for the owner view.

The web administration table is  /admin/registration-audit . It derives the
allowlist from current administrator roles, revalidates every gateway row, uses
25-row pages, and returns  Cache-Control: no-store . There is deliberately no
CSV or other export route: out-of-scope filters are denied before the gateway is
queried, and partial-scope results are never rendered.

The server-facing protocol conformance and denied-state matrix run with:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdater-enrollment
cargo test -p fdupdater-enrollment --test denied_states
cargo test -p fdupdate-device-gateway

title: Self-hosting
text:
Self-host FDUpdate Server

The supported deployment is one Linux host with the FDUpdate TLS edge/services,
Eclipse hawkBit 1.1.0, and MariaDB on private container networks. Review
  server-deployment.md   server-deployment.md  first.

1. Provision a dedicated DNS name and host; expose only TCP 443.
2. Check out and verify an exact FDUpdate release.
3. Keep root-owned config/state outside source and executable trees. Provide TLS,
   database, operator, signing, OIDC, and storage secrets through protected files.
4. Run  server/deploy/fdupdate-server init-config , then  validate ,  install ,
    public-tls , and  acceptance  with the documented absolute path arguments.
5. Verify TLS health/enrollment and confirm hawkBit, MariaDB, Management API,
   administration, and diagnostics are not publicly reachable.

Create encrypted consistent database/state backups and an immutable artifact
inventory. Restore into isolation and smoke-test enrollment, metadata, download,
rollout, feedback, and operators. Test upgrades against a restored backup. When
schema rollback is incompatible, restore the whole pre-upgrade recovery point.

See  deployment  server-deployment.md ,  operations  runtime-operations.md ,
 recovery  server-recovery.md , and  retention  release-retention.md .

title: Operator API
text:
Server operator API and CLI

 fdupdate-server-api  defines the versioned operator request/response contract used by loopback, mTLS or OIDC transports. Credentials are redacted, stored as hashes and compared without content-dependent early exit. Actors receive explicit roles and tenant/product scopes.

Security administrators register products and approve or revoke installations. Release managers publish immutable releases. Fleet operators start, pause, resume or abort rollouts. Readers access bounded status and diagnostics. A valid role never grants another product scope.

Every request ID is bound to the actor and action. An exact retry returns the original response without a second effect; reuse with another action fails. Authorized, denied and failed first decisions enter a SHA-256 hash-chained audit containing actor, action, scope, result and effect ID, without credentials.

 parse_cli_action  exposes the matching CLI grammar. The transport reads credentials from protected files and supplies them separately; the CLI grammar deliberately has no credential argument.

Focused verification:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdate-server-api --test conformance --locked
cargo clippy -p fdupdate-server-api --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

title: Security
text:
Security and trust model

Networks and distribution are untrusted. Product-scoped Ed25519 keys authenticate
canonical releases and artifacts. Sequence, compatibility, platform, rollout,
dependency, installed-version and exact rollback rules are checked locally. Size
and SHA-256 are verified before staging. Private signing keys never belong to the
updater or a long-running server.

Enrollment binds one public key, instance and tenant/product scope. Pending,
denied, revoked, wrong-scope, replayed, or ungranted installations receive no
metadata or bytes. Operators have individual roles/scopes, short sessions, CSRF
protection, and audit. Secrets use protected files/providers, never releases,
browser storage, command arguments, or logs. Store failures deny delivery.

The supported Linux deployment separates the public device gateway from the web
owner runtime by UID, primary group, secret directory and mutable state. Their
only shared filesystem authority is group read access to the Installation Account
document and advisory-lock access to one root-provisioned lock file in a directory
neither service can modify. The gateway therefore keeps account authority stable
through delegated enrollment without gaining write access to account,
self-service or administrator state and without access to administrator, COT or
web operator credentials.

title: Backup and recovery
text:
FDUpdate Server backup, observation and recovery

The recovery archive contains product IDs, approved target IDs, release artifact digests, rollout state and non-secret configuration metadata. It excludes credentials, private keys, secret configuration values and artifact payloads. The archive binds its canonical payload with SHA-256; recovery verifies the complete payload before the operator replaces the last known-good state.

Operational metrics are counters for health failures, rollout pauses, storage use and backup failures. The bounded observation window accepts only compact category/outcome labels and evicts the oldest entry at its configured limit. It does not accept request bodies, credentials or arbitrary log messages.

Credential and signing-key rotation uses distinct key IDs. During the documented overlap deadline, current and previous credentials remain valid; expiry or explicit revocation rejects the old identity. A failed rotation leaves the current identity recoverable. Private signing material remains in the isolated signer and is restored or rotated by its external key-custody procedure, not from a server backup.

title: Versioning
text:
Versioning and compatibility

FDTasks progress uses  MAJOR.RELEASE.EPIC.ITEM ; release tags identify executable
releases. Rust crates have no stable binary ABI, so pin source revisions.

Persisted and exchanged contracts carry exact schema IDs. Unknown versions and
fields fail closed. Compatibility changes use a new schema or explicit migration;
old state is never guessed. Client/server compatibility follows protocol/schema
versions and signed minimum-updater requirements, not matching package versions.
Release notes identify migration and rollback impact; validate upgrades against a
restored backup. See  CHANGELOG.md  and  self-hosting  self-hosting.md .

The immutable v1 wire rules, exact platform/ABI matching and release/prerelease
selection are defined in the  unified release protocol  unified-release-protocol.md .

title: COT integration
text:
COT service-client integration

FDUpdate Server consumes the current standalone COT service contract rather
than embedding COT. The workspace pins COT commit
 9f720a6ed5a68dd1fa5df5716fdf7bea57e67c0e , disables default features and
enables only  cot-sdk/service-client .

The trusted boundary is  LocalChannelClient :

- it accepts loopback HTTP endpoints only;
- it authenticates with a protected application service credential;
- channel administration uses  cot.private-channels/v1 ;
- Telegram setup is write-only and provider secrets remain in COT;
- list/get/delete use owner-private opaque resources and ETags;
- delivery uses  send_private_message  with stable idempotency and correlation
  identities.

Installation Account email self-service additionally uses COT-0473's published
 cot.private-email-dynamic-recipient/v1  contract: one application-private
channel binds the protected sender/provider setup, and each send supplies one
validated recipient. FDUpdate uses the typed SDK pinned above and verifies it
against a conforming fake COT service. The project owner confirmed the pinned
candidate's complete upstream test/conformance result and deployment. The
authorized VPS deployment manifest binds the same commit and the running binary
digest; its live health probe passes. FDUpdate's focused typed-fixture, security,
UI and deployment verification therefore governs compatibility even while the
upstream work item remains open for an unrelated lifecycle reason.

 NotificationRuntime  owns only FDUpdate's bounded routing/handoff file. COT
owns its service database, provider adapters, destination data and process
lifecycle. Stopping FDUpdate drops the HTTP client; it must not stop the shared
COT service.

Updating COT requires an accepted maintenance task, a full immutable source
revision, lockfile update and focused adapter/web tests against the new public
contract. Read current COT sources and contract documentation from the COT
repository; do not copy private implementation details or modify that
repository.

Production COT credentials, bot tokens and chat IDs remain outside this
repository. Use an isolated loopback fixture for automated verification and a
separately authorized environment for any explicitly approved live delivery
check.

title: License
text:
FDUpdate license decision

Status:   approved by the project owner on 2026-10-18  .

The owner selected   Apache License 2.0   for FDUpdater, the embeddable libraries,
FDUpdate-owned server code, examples and documentation. Apache-2.0 provides an
explicit patent grant and termination terms and permits commercial use, including
competing hosted services. An OSI-approved license cannot promise to exclude such
competition.

Alternatives considered:

- Apache-2.0 alone keeps the patent terms but removes the simple MIT option.
- MIT alone is simple but lacks Apache-2.0's express patent language.
- AGPL-3.0 requires corresponding source for modified network deployments and
  may deter proprietary hosted forks, but adds integration/compliance friction
  and is not compatible with every intended embedding policy.

The locked Rust dependency graph currently has complete declared license/source
metadata and uses permissive expressions  MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib,
Unicode, CC0/CDLA-Permissive and compatible alternatives . COT is  MIT OR
Apache-2.0 . Eclipse hawkBit remains a separate unmodified EPL-2.0 service; its
license/notices travel with its image and are not relicensed by FDUpdate.

The repository carries the full terms in root  LICENSE , workspace package
metadata uses SPDX  Apache-2.0 , and  THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md  identifies separately
licensed dependencies and services. Contributions are offered under Apache-2.0.
Repository visibility remains separately controlled by the publication checklist.

title: Contributing
text:
Contributing

Contributions are licensed under Apache License 2.0. Contributors must have the
right to provide them. Never include credentials, customer data, private keys, or
production configuration.

Discuss material protocol changes first; read  AGENTS.md  and  DEVELOPMENT.md ;
use the pinned toolchain; run formatting, affected tests, Clippy with warnings
denied, and  node scripts/check-public-docs.mjs  for docs changes. Pull requests
describe behavior, compatibility/security impact, and exact validation. Report
vulnerabilities privately through  SECURITY.md .

title: Support
text:
Support

Use GitHub Discussions for questions and Issues for reproducible defects. Include
version, OS, component, sanitized logs, expected behavior, and exact CLI steps.
Remove secrets, private URLs, customer data, and signing material. Community
support is best-effort; no SLA, managed hosting, paid plan, or emergency response
is currently offered. Security reports follow  SECURITY.md .

title: FDUpdate release storage architecture — FDFiles protected object interface
text:
FDUpdate release storage architecture — FDFiles protected object interface

Status: owner-directed successor for FDU-EPIC-D010 implementation. The accepted
v1 S3 architecture remains immutable historical input.

   Boundary

FDUpdate uses the versioned FDFiles v1 integration API as its primary protected
store/read boundary. FDUpdate does not receive S3 credentials, bucket names,
provider object keys or storage-placement authority. A short-lived service token
is supplied by an external secret provider and is sent only to the configured
HTTPS control origin.

The implementation is pinned to FDFiles wire version  1  and canonical OpenAPI
SHA-256  38dc1b30cbff265d6944f1b37e9168cba64a9155f058a04d131ab85d573e2bf8 .
That contract belongs to the accepted FDFiles D040 product candidate
 932daf9b9d3d1e6075dd6dc490c2b8f0c9557bfd   tree
 2d392f1027b0efd5dec89b5333b6e7f673179ade   and was inspected read-only in the
FDFiles repository. Its D040 gate and independent review are closed. The public
FDFiles  origin/main  still points to the earlier  9328891  contract and is not
deployment-compatible with mirror deletion; production configuration must use
an accepted FDFiles build containing D040 or a compatible successor.

The unpublished prototype SDK is not copied or linked: its repository license
allows packaging metadata only and forbids distribution without owner approval.
FDUpdate implements the bounded HTTP operations required by this architecture.

Service-token issuance follows the normative OpenAPI scopes, not older prose:
uploads require  resources:write , resource reads and download sessions require
 resources:read , revision-bound deletion requires  resources:delete , and all
durable-operation polling requires  operations:read . FDUpdate requests these
exact scope identities from its external token source and requires separate
protected regular token files for least-privilege operation. It does not use the
obsolete  files:read  or  files:write  names. Different spellings of one path
are canonicalized before the CLI accepts them as separate scope files.

   Immutable identity

Every stored artifact is identified by its SHA-256, exact byte length, media
type and the SHA-256 of the signed release manifest that authorizes it. The
portable content key is  sha256/<first-two-hex>/<full-digest> . FDFiles resource
and revision IDs are opaque locators, never authority or artifact identity.

Publication creates a checksummed upload session, transfers bounded chunks,
completes the session and accepts only a returned resource whose size and digest
match the immutable identity. Retrieval pins the exact resource revision in a
download session, validates range responses and verifies the complete digest
before atomic activation by a caller.

   Security and failure behavior

- Control and data clients reject redirects. Authorization is sent only to the
  control origin; data-plane requests receive only the headers returned for the
  exact capability URL.
- Production origins require HTTPS. Plain HTTP is allowed only for an explicit
  loopback test configuration.
- Requests, retries, chunks, responses, operation polling and total artifact
  size are bounded. Uncertain mutations retain stable idempotency keys.
- Authentication, authorization, version, revision, size and integrity failures
  fail closed and never create a trusted locator.
- The local backend uses the same identity contract and atomically installs a
  verified content-addressed file without following links.

   Revision-bound deletion and remaining distribution boundary

Accepted FDFiles D040 resolves the earlier resource-delete contract gap.
 DELETE /v1/resources/{resource_id}?revision=...  requires a stable
 Idempotency-Key  and a  resources:delete  token. A stale revision fails without
admitting deletion. FDUpdate accepts completion only from the exact durable
 delete_resource  operation, polled with  operations:read ; retries use a key
derived from the journal operation and exact opaque locator. The SDK licensing
boundary remains, so no FDFiles package is distributed or linked.

FDU-141 does not delete resources. Its  fdupdate-storage publish-stage  CLI
publishes one verified artifact to primary FDFiles, retrieves it through a
read-scoped download session into an immutable VPS content object, then
atomically advances a per-product/channel/platform/architecture/variant index.
The prior index target remains the known-good fallback. Configuration names
separate  read_token_file ,  write_token_file  and
 operations_read_token_file ; all must be protected regular files outside the
repository. A primary success followed by cache failure is reported as failure
and is safe to retry under artifact-derived idempotency keys.

   Delayed mirror mutation journal

FDU-143 adds the canonical  fdupdate/mirror-mutation-journal/v1  state. Each
bounded operation records an immutable ID, create/replace/delete kind, exact
primary artifact identity and FDFiles revision, expected mirror revision when
applicable, policy version, primary confirmation time and a computed
 not_before  exactly 24 hours later. The journal is atomically persisted behind
a separate process lock, rejects symlinks, duplicate IDs, noncanonical state and
files larger than 16 MiB, and caps entries at 100,000.

 fdupdate-storage mirror-enqueue JOURNAL REQUEST.json  records a confirmed
primary mutation. Replaying an identical immutable request returns the existing
operation; changed input under the same ID conflicts. Enqueueing never contacts
or activates a mirror.  fdupdate-storage mirror-status JOURNAL REQUEST.json 
returns either the operation selected by optional  operation_id  or the bounded
complete journal, including durable state, attempts and an explicit failure
classification.

 fdupdate-storage mirror-execute CONFIG.json REQUEST.json  is the only execution
entry point.  CONFIG.json  must explicitly set  enabled: true , provide distinct
primary and mirror endpoint configurations and non-reused credential files, a
real staging directory, the journal path and a separate protected regular
 authority_public_key_file . The executor never receives the authority private
key. With  enabled: false , the operation stays pending. Endpoint token files are
optional in the common schema but the attempted HTTP operation fails closed
unless its exact  resources:read ,  resources:write ,  resources:delete  or
 operations:read  token file is configured.

FDU-180 replaces caller-authored revalidation assertions with
 fdupdate/mirror-decision/v1 . The execution request contains only a canonical
base64 payload and Ed25519 signature. The domain-separated payload binds a unique
decision and trusted key ID, operation ID and kind, policy version, exact Primary
and expected Mirror identities/revisions, authorization and deletion eligibility,
retention and last-restorable-backup protection, issue time and expiry. The
configured public-key document has schema
 fdupdate/mirror-authority-key/v1 ; unknown keys, noncanonical encodings and bad
signatures fail before any remote request.

An initial decision must be issued after the full hold, be neither future nor
expired and remain within five minutes of execution. Create and replace require
the authoritative exact Primary and Mirror state, then download and verify the
Primary bytes before a checksummed create or revision-bound replace. Delete
requires authoritative Primary absence, explicit eligibility, no retention pin
and confirmation that the object is not the last restorable database backup.
Changed, unauthorized or protected work is rejected or durably cancelled without
remote mutation.

Before remote mutation the journal records  running , the decision ID, the digest
of the exact signed envelope and  not_issued . The FDFiles adapter then classifies
