title: FDUpdate release storage architecture — primary S3, future mirror, VPS latest-copy cache
text:
FDUpdate release storage architecture — primary S3, future mirror, VPS latest-copy cache

Status: owner-approved target architecture; implementation and live migration not started.

   Storage tiers
1. Primary: Hetzner Object Storage S3 or compatible alternative; immutable content-addressed artifacts and signed manifests for every retained release and prerelease.
2. Secondary: independent S3 mirror  prefer distinct provider/region and failure domain ,   planned but not deployed now  ; eventually replicate all retained versions, with verified object checksums and delayed/versioned deletion protection.
3. Local VPS: verified latest stable release and latest prerelease   per product, channel, OS, architecture and required package variant  , not just one global file. VPS copies are both recovery cache and last-known-good fallback; reserve sufficient disk and capacity alerts.

   Publication and activation
- CI manual publish uploads to Primary, validates digest/size/signature and commits immutable catalog metadata.
- Stage the new latest package to VPS and verify it before evicting prior local copy; maintain at least one previously known-good candidate during replacement.
- Define clear readiness semantics: publishing a release may be blocked or marked degraded if latest VPS copy is not safely present; never claim three replicas before mirror activation.
- When mirror is enabled, asynchronous replication has tracked pending/verified/failed states and alerts. Never infer successful mirror write from a queued job.
- Manifest/catalog metadata, encryption/signing keys, installation registry and DB require   separate backup and restore  , not merely artifact copies.

   Download and failure
- Primary direct download with short-lived authorized URL for private artifacts; fallback to independently verified Mirror when enabled.
- If both S3 locations unavailable, latest local VPS copy can be served through authenticated FDUpdate gateway with strict bandwidth/concurrency/rate limits.
- Older versions are unavailable during primary outage until mirror is enabled; avoid claiming always-on service: VPS/network/API are shared failure domains.
- Every fallback verifies exact immutable artifact digest and signed manifest; no downgrade or private-to-public disclosure.
- Health checks, reconciliation, periodic scrub, orphan cleanup, corruption quarantine and restore drills.

   Retention and deletion
- Configurable stable/prerelease retention per repository  default 10 each from existing requirements .
- Pin latest local variants and all objects required by active rollout/rollback; stage replacements atomically.
- Mirror deletion must not blindly propagate accidental primary deletion; use object versioning or protected deletion grace and restore process.
- Account for VPS local disk, primary/mirror storage, egress, request charges and API proxy costs.

   Proposed FDTasks successor scope
- Storage provider abstraction and S3 backend.
- Atomic primary publication and local latest-copy cache.
- Fallback download selection, integrity and access control.
- Mirroring interface and replication journal  future mirror inactive .
- Scrub, retention, metadata backups, restore and failure tests.
- Admin dashboard showing replica health, cache occupancy, per-release copies, alerts and costs.
- One targeted gate and independent review under a next development Epic; avoid modifying accepted D009 task specs and follow FDTasks 5.5 append-only rules.

No production DNS, S3 credentials, live releases or billing changed by this document.


   Owner-approved 24-hour delayed mirror and database backup policy  2026-10-18 
- VPS holds the live database. Create consistent, encrypted, restorable database backups in Primary S3, including required catalog, enrollment and installation metadata; replicate backups to Mirror S3.
-   Every mirror mutation  create, overwrite where permitted, and delete  executes no earlier than 24 hours after the corresponding primary operation has been durably confirmed and validated.   Queue an immutable operation record with source object version/digest, primary confirmation timestamp and mirror-not-before timestamp.
- At execution time revalidate source object version, cryptographic digest, authorization, retention pins and current deletion eligibility. Stale or superseded operations must be cancelled/reconciled, not blindly replayed.
- Mirror deletes require verified primary deletion eligibility and independent second check after the full delay; do not delete the last known restorable database backup or protected release.
- The delay applies to new backups as well: mirror recovery point may be at least 24 hours behind primary. Protect this window with Primary S3 object versioning/immutability and local database WAL/snapshot retention; do not advertise zero data loss.
- A 24-hour delayed mirror is a replication target,   not   a complete backup defense against ransomware or credential compromise. Use separate credentials, versioning/Object Lock where supported, restore drills and tested offsite recovery.
- Monitor replication queue age, lag, failed verification, backup age, restore success and retained storage size. Make the delay configurable only through a future explicit policy change; initial mandatory minimum is 24 hours.
- No live mirror is provisioned in this phase; preserve interfaces and migration plan.

title: SaaS-ready foundations
text:
SaaS-ready foundations

FDUpdate remains a self-hosted, single-organization product. The
 fdupdate-saas-foundation  crate defines extension contracts needed by a future
managed service without adding signup, billing, pricing, or cloud dependencies.

Every application, repository, release, installation key, installation, feedback
record, artifact, and audit event has one validated organization owner. Existing
server  tenant  plus repository/product scope is the current ownership source.
Authorization compares trusted session/credential scope with stored ownership;
client-supplied tenant text never grants access. Colliding IDs across organizations
remain distinct and failures deny access.

 StorageBackend  binds immutable SHA-256/length identities to organization-owned
objects. The local backend stays the default. An S3-compatible implementation must
pass the same identity, immutability, ownership, corruption, and unavailable-store
contract before selection; bucket/object URLs never become authorization.

 UsageLedger  accepts organization-scoped idempotent event IDs and counts stored
bytes, egress bytes, and registered installations.  Quota  can deny a proposed
delta before effect. These are policy hooks, not billing records; they contain no
price, payment, invoice, customer secret, or mandatory remote call.

Legacy state migrates only with an administrator-selected default organization.
The migration writes explicit owners, validates the result, and retains the
pre-migration backup for rollback. It never infers multiple organizations from
product names, repositories, hostnames, or credentials.

title: Client feedback
text:
Client feedback

Integrated applications use  fdupdate-feedback  to create feedback or bug reports and keep a bounded durable retry queue. The application supplies its own current target and installed version from the same local receipt/registry it uses for update checks. It never accepts an installation ID, tenant or repository from the user. The gateway derives those values from the authenticated installation credential and its last reported application state.

   rust,no_run
use fdupdate_feedback::{FeedbackKind, FeedbackQueue, FeedbackRequest};

  fn example state_root: &std::path::Path, target: fdupdate_contract::Target,
             installed: fdupdate_contract::Version  -> fdupdate_feedback::Result<  > {
let request = FeedbackRequest::new 
    "ui-20261018-0001",
    target,
    FeedbackKind::Bug,
    "Window does not open",
    "Opening the main window leaves the process in the background.",
    1_792_300_000,
    installed,
    None, // diagnostics require an explicit Some ... 
 ?;
FeedbackQueue::open state_root ?.enqueue request ?;
  Ok     }
   

A transport submits the oldest queued request as JSON to  POST /v1/feedback/{tenant}/{product}  with the installation credential as Bearer authorization and  X-FDUpdate-Instance .  submit_next  removes a request only after the transport accepts it and the shorter queue is durably committed. A transient outage leaves the original request ID and submitted version intact for an idempotent retry.

The request is limited to a 160-byte subject, 8 KiB body, three explicitly opted-in text diagnostics, 16 KiB per diagnostic and 32 KiB total diagnostic text. Diagnostic labels are basename-only. Both the client constructor and server store redact complete lines containing authorization, password, secret, token or credential markers. The adapter never reads host files automatically.

The server authenticates the installation and component, requires prior reported installed state, and records the client-reported version beside the server's last-known installed version. It labels them match, mismatch or unknown and never substitutes an assigned or available release. Tenant, installation, repository, platform, architecture and channel are server-derived. A changed reuse of a request ID conflicts; an exact retry returns  accepted: false . New reports are limited to 20 per installation per hour and the durable store is bounded to 100,000 records.

The client request ID is idempotency provenance within one installation. On first acceptance the server derives a separate stable report ID from the tenant, product, installation and client request ID. Operator URLs, workflow mutations, duplicate links and audit use that server report ID, so two installations may safely choose the same client request ID. Current gateway and feedback snapshots require their feedback section and every workflow field. Explicit schema-1 migration derives the same stable IDs and rejects ambiguous legacy duplicate links; malformed current snapshots fail before state becomes visible.

HTTP responses use 401 for invalid/revoked identity, 409 for missing installed state or changed duplicate, 429 for the per-installation rate limit, 507 for exhausted durable capacity and 503 when the atomic gateway snapshot cannot be committed.
   Administrator inbox

Owners, fleet operators and security administrators open  /admin/feedback . The server requests only products represented by repositories visible to the account and filters each report again by its server-derived repository. The inbox supports bounded search, status/type filters and 25-record pages. Report details link to the exact installation and repository and keep the original reported version beside the current server-last-known version.

Workflow changes use the stable server report ID, the report's current revision and the administrator session CSRF token. New, In progress, Resolved and Closed status, internal notes and same-repository duplicate links persist in the gateway snapshot. A stale revision returns conflict. Original subject, body, version, identity, timestamps and diagnostics never change; every workflow mutation appends actor/time/status/note metadata to a bounded audit trail. Restoration reconciles each note with exactly one audit revision, enforces ordered server timestamps and rejects self-links or duplicate cycles. All client text, diagnostic names/content and note text are HTML-escaped. The page uses  Cache-Control: no-store  and switches filters and workflow controls to one column below 600 px.

title: COT service notifications
text:
COT service notifications

FDUpdate Server uses  cot-sdk  at immutable COT revision
 dd7496c14bf3526fd93d8b92c00ede34f8ae3c05  with default features disabled
and only  service-client  enabled. FDUpdate does not embed a COT provider,
open a COT database, or own the COT process lifecycle.

Enable notifications by setting all three values in the protected
 fdupdate-web  JSON configuration:

   json
{
  "notification_state_dir": "/var/lib/fdupdate/notifications",
  "cot_service_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8081/",
  "cot_service_credential_file": "/etc/fdupdate/cot-service.credential"
}
   

The endpoint must be loopback. The credential file must be a regular,
non-symlink file no larger than 512 bytes and readable only by the FDUpdate
service account. COT must authorize that credential as the FDUpdate application.
Production credentials, provider secrets and destination identifiers stay
outside this repository.

Owners create Telegram channels from  /admin/notifications . FDUpdate passes
the write-only bot token and chat ID into COT private-channel protected setup;
COT owns the secret, destination, channel lifecycle and provider deduplication.
FDUpdate stores and displays only COT's opaque channel ID, safe display label,
lifecycle state, revision and ETag. It can list, test and conditionally delete
its own private channels. Stale ETags fail closed.

FDUpdate persists a bounded event-to-COT handoff before calling
 send_private_message . A logical message ID binds the event, route, opaque
channel ID and channel ETag, so equal ETags on different COT channels cannot
collide. The event ID is also passed as correlation ID. Each attempt rechecks
that the channel is still ready with the exact bound identity and revision.
Changed or removed authority cancels unsent work rather than retargeting it.

States are  queued ,  retrying ,  in_flight ,  sent ,  uncertain ,
 failed ,  expired  and  cancelled .  sent  means COT reported provider
acceptance or an already-processed idempotent message; it is not proof that a
person read it. Timeout or transport loss after a send is  uncertain  because
the provider may already have accepted the message. Operator retry retains the
same logical identity and can still duplicate at a provider that cannot
guarantee idempotency.

The handoff remains limited to 4096 jobs, 64 jobs per pass, five admitted
attempts, 4096 message bytes and 24 hours lifetime. Feedback and update
transactions never depend on COT availability. Rules remain disabled on first
creation, previews do not send, repository-scoped administrators see only
authorized rule/history projections, and all browser mutations require a valid
session and CSRF value.

Legacy v1/v2 embedded-COT handoff files upgrade to v3. Nonterminal legacy jobs
are cancelled with  cot_service_migration_required ; provider credentials and
destinations are deliberately not imported from the old embedded state.

title: DAF validation publication and update flow
text:
DAF validation publication and update flow

DAF source revision  09ea5125e2a55f21bd231fd077d5cc8a7c2d7b9b  adds an opt-in  publish_fdupdate_validation  input to its existing manual build workflow. The job runs only after the application build and persistence jobs succeed, uses the protected  fdupdate-validation  environment and requests  id-token: write . It prepares exact publication plans locally in the job and submits a Linux x86-64 DAF application package and the checked-in BAW master firmware package to separate publisher IDs.

The validation server must register these publishers with the same exact GitHub issuer, repository  fedrnv/DAF , workflow ref  fedrnv/DAF/.github/workflows/daf.yml@refs/heads/main , environment  fdupdate-validation , main ref, audience  fdupdate-server  and  workflow_dispatch  event:

-  daf-application : product  daf , component  application , target  linux/x86_64 .
-  daf-baw-master : product  daf , component  controller-firmware , target  linux/baw-master .

The protected environment variable  FDUPDATE_PUBLISH_URL  must be a credential-free HTTPS origin. The workflow obtains its short-lived OIDC token from the GitHub runtime, submits it only in the Authorization header and unsets the shell value after both requests. Plans bind the DAF Git commit, workflow recipe digest, versions, sizes and SHA-256 artifact digests. The server signs and commits each release independently; a wrong firmware architecture such as  hsd-master  is outside the publisher scope.

The DAF application keeps its existing update dialogs and BAW firmware mechanism. An enrolled installation remains unable to check or download while pending. After explicit approval, the application assignment targets  daf/application  and the firmware assignment targets  daf/controller-firmware ; the BAW master identity is carried by publication compatibility/architecture metadata. Reports use the accepted application-managed flow and are idempotent.

The Linux validation foundation is installed on the dedicated server at  update.fedrv.de  with a trusted public TLS edge. Only the exact publisher ingestion path is public; hawkBit Management and operator boundaries remain private. Hardware acceptance requires an accessible supported BAW master controller; simulator results are not hardware evidence.

title: Enrollment codes and installation identities
text:
Enrollment codes and installation identities

The installation identity page in  fdupdate-server-panel  uses the existing security-administrator role and exact tenant/product scope. It lists installation ID, product, assigned component target, public-key fingerprint, enrollment state, creation time, last successful authenticated-seen time and revocation state. The response contains no private key, access credential, enrollment-code verifier or reusable secret.

A security administrator may issue a code for one registered product/component and an expiry from 60 seconds through 24 hours. The server generates 256 random bits, returns the lowercase hexadecimal plaintext on a one-time response page and persists only a domain-separated SHA-256 verifier plus code ID, scope, issue/expiry time and usage state. Operator and registry audit trails record issuance without plaintext.

The installation generates and retains its Ed25519 private key locally. A rate-limited enrollment submission must match the code scope and expiry. Successful consumption and creation of the pending identity commit together in the registry snapshot; it does not approve the identity or return targets or an access credential. Wrong-scope, expired, invalid and reused codes fail closed.

Revocation verifies the selected public-key fingerprint, disables the hawkBit target and removes the server-side credential hash before the audited panel action succeeds. Registry authentication then denies status/report access, and the delivery authorizer denies metadata and artifact requests. Reusing the old request with a fresh code cannot restore a revoked public-key identity.

CLI transports use  enrollment-code-issue TENANT PRODUCT COMPONENT EXPIRES_UNIX ,  installation-list TENANT PRODUCT  and the existing  installation-revoke TENANT PRODUCT INSTANCE FINGERPRINT REASON  operator actions.

The live  /admin  transport applies the authenticated session and CSRF check
before calling the private device-gateway operator API. It shows the current
fingerprint, state, last-seen time and repository grants, and exposes separate
approve, deny, identity revoke, repository grant and repository revoke actions.
The web service receives only the gateway operator token copied into its own
root-owned secret directory; that token is never rendered or sent to a browser.

The panel issues the one-time plaintext through
 POST /admin/installations/enrollment-code . A standalone target may provision it
in  enrollment.code_file ; FDUpdater sends it only in the protected enrollment
request together with the exact component ID. The gateway atomically consumes
the persistent verifier and creates a pending identity. Exact retries from that
same cryptographic request remain idempotent, while a different installation,
wrong component, expired code or malformed code is rejected. Approval and
repository grant remain two explicit later browser actions.

   Reusable installation keys

A security administrator with complete repository authority for a product can
create and manage reusable installation keys on  /admin . The create form records
a display name, product and component scope, repository allowlist, optional
expiry, and an installation limit. The limit defaults to one and accepts bounded
values such as 1, 10, or 100. The generated plaintext key is returned once in a
 no-store  response. The dashboard and gateway subsequently expose only its
stable identifier and verifier-backed metadata.

Each key card shows its creator, state, expiry, used and remaining quota, current
repository allowlist, and the immutable registration history. Registration rows
identify the independently generated installation identity and whether it was
revoked. Quota counts distinct successful registrations; an exact retry does not
consume another slot, and lowering the limit never deletes historical usage.

Editing a key can rename it, change its repository allowlist, or raise or lower
its quota.  Disable new enrollment  stops admission while preserving inherited
access for existing installations.  Suspend inherited update access  separately
removes the key's repository authority from every derived installation until an
administrator restores it. Individual installation revocation remains available
through the existing fingerprint-confirmed action and does not revoke sibling
installations.

All installation-key actions require an authenticated security-administrator
session, a valid CSRF token, and complete product repository scope. The web
service checks submitted product, repository, and key identifiers against its
bounded authoritative inventory before calling the private gateway routes:
 POST /v1/operator/installation-keys ,
 POST /v1/operator/installation-keys/list , and
 POST /v1/operator/installation-keys/update .

title: GitHub Actions publication
text:
GitHub Actions publication

An administrator first creates the update repository in the FDUpdate administrator panel. Creation fixes a stable project key, public/private visibility, product/component scope and one exact GitHub repository, workflow reference, protected environment and allowed ref. This repository record is the publisher authority; no second deployment registration is required. The panel displays the generated publishing secret once; the server stores only its repository- and generation-bound verifier. Rotation immediately invalidates the old secret and revocation denies publication until a new generation is issued.

The publishing job requests a short-lived GitHub Actions OIDC token. FDUpdate selects the token's current key ID from GitHub's HTTPS JWKS and accepts only an RS256 signature plus exact claims for issuer  https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com , audience, repository,  workflow_ref , environment, ref, commit  sha  and  event_name=workflow_dispatch . The token lifetime is at most ten minutes. The token and its  jti  are never written to audit; only a SHA-256 token identifier is held for request processing.

The HTTPS request must contain  x-fdupdate-project-key ,  x-fdupdate-publishing-secret ,  x-fdupdate-source-revision  and  x-fdupdate-publication-comment  together with  x-fdupdate-request-id  and the OIDC bearer token. The source revision must equal the signed OIDC  sha  claim. The publishing secret belongs in a protected GitHub environment secret and must never be printed; project key and comment may be workflow inputs. The gateway validates the JWT header, current repository credential and exact signed GitHub identity before consuming multipart fields. The bounded canonical plan must be the first field and pass repository scope validation before the artifact field is opened. Missing, unknown, mismatched, rotated or revoked values therefore create no artifact staging.

After dual authorization, the versioned ingestion request supplies a canonical publication plan and one bounded artifact stream. The gateway permits one artifact stream at a time, bounding concurrent staging to one maximum-size artifact and releasing capacity on every response. The artifact must match the server repository and registered product, component, platform and architecture. When provenance is required, the gateway verifies its attestation before the isolated signer verifies the digest and signs the release. The publication backend prepares hawkBit state before the immutable store becomes visible. Commit failure invokes abort and removes staged and final output. The gateway journals request fingerprints, receipts and a queryable provenance record containing project, publisher, GitHub repository, exact source SHA, time, bounded comment, release and artifact hashes. An exact request-ID retry after process restart returns the original receipt; changed SHA, comment, project or plan conflicts. Corrupt state prevents startup.

Application workflows may build, package and publish only when manually started with  workflow_dispatch . They do not execute FDUpdate acceptance tests. Installation enrollment credentials, hawkBit Management credentials and signing private keys never enter GitHub Actions.

   Build provenance admission

Build provenance is opt-in per publisher. With no provenance configuration, or for an absent publisher entry, publication keeps the existing flow and records  provenance_not_required . A required entry never downgrades: a missing, empty, malformed, untrusted or larger-than-2-MiB bundle is rejected before release signing. Supplying an attestation when policy is disabled is also rejected, so producer and server policy changes are deliberate.

The policy file has schema  fdupdate/publisher-provenance-policy/v1 . A required policy pins the stable numeric GitHub repository ID, the approved builder ID and the feature availability decision:

   json
{
  "schema": "fdupdate/publisher-provenance-policy/v1",
  "policies": {
    "example-publisher": {
      "mode": "required",
      "version": "github-private-v1",
      "repository_id": 123456789,
      "builder_id": "https://github.com/actions/runner/github-hosted",
      "availability": "private_enterprise_cloud"
    }
  }
}
   

Allowed availability values are  public_repository ,  private_enterprise_cloud  and  private_unsupported . GitHub supports attestations for public repositories on current plans, but private or internal repositories require GitHub Enterprise Cloud.  private_unsupported  is an explicit fail-closed decision, not a disabled policy. Obtain and review the numeric ID independently  for example,  gh api repos/OWNER/REPOSITORY --jq .id  ; repository names alone do not survive rename and name reuse safely.

The server provenance configuration points to that policy and, when at least one supported entry is required, to a verifier configuration. FDUpdate currently accepts GitHub CLI  2.101.0  under the MIT license. Operators pin the executable path, its SHA-256, exact version, trusted-root JSONL path and SHA-256, root generation time, maximum root age and verifier timeout. The configured maximum root age cannot exceed 30 days. Startup fails if the executable/version/hash or root/hash is wrong. Every admission rechecks the root age and the pinned files' size and modification identity.

Verification is offline and fail-closed. The server invokes the pinned CLI with the supplied bundle and custom root while network proxy variables point to a closed local endpoint and credential variables are removed. It enforces the exact artifact SHA-256, SLSA provenance v1 predicate, numeric repository ID, GitHub-hosted builder, exact workflow certificate identity, source commit and ref. This supplements the product-scoped release signature; it does not prove source correctness or claim a SLSA level.

Generate a fresh combined public/private root snapshot on an online administrative machine with  gh attestation trusted-root > trusted_root.jsonl , record its digest and generation time, then transfer it through the deployment's trusted configuration channel. GitHub's root metadata has no built-in expiry. Offline verification cannot know about revocations after the snapshot, and material signed after the snapshot may stop verifying after key rotation; rotate the configured snapshot deliberately and keep policy/version changes auditable.

For a required policy, multipart fields are strictly ordered:  plan ,  artifact ,  attestation , with no trailing field. The attestation is the JSONL emitted by  gh attestation download ARTIFACT -R OWNER/REPOSITORY . Disabled policy continues to accept exactly  plan ,  artifact . A successful required admission stores an immutable compact receipt and retains the bundle by SHA-256 under the publication store. Exact replay, including after restart, reuses that receipt without rerunning the verifier or signer; changed artifact, bundle, root or policy conflicts. Failed signing/publication removes a newly retained bundle.

An application repository may add the following step to its existing manual-only build job. Keep the workflow trigger as  workflow_dispatch , grant  id-token: write ,  contents: read  and  attestations: write , and pin the action by full commit rather than a floating tag:

   yaml
- name: Attest release artifact
  uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6   v4.2.2
  with:
    subject-path: dist/fdos-update.zip

- name: Download bundle for FDUpdate upload
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  run: gh attestation download dist/fdos-update.zip -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
   

Pass the generated  sha256: .jsonl  file as the  attestation  multipart field in the same authenticated FDUpdate request as the exact artifact. Attestation generation and bundle download occur only inside that explicitly dispatched producer workflow; FDUpdate's verifier performs no public-networ

title: Open-source publication readiness
text:
Open-source publication readiness

FDUpdate remains private until the owner authorizes the exact license and GitHub
visibility change. Run the local baseline audit from a clean checkout:

   text
node scripts/audit-public-readiness.mjs
gitleaks git --config .gitleaks.toml --redact --no-banner
   

The audit covers tracked secret/state file names, the complete locked Rust graph,
contributor identities and hosted workflow triggers. Gitleaks scans the complete
Git history. Its two narrow allowlists cover only immutable disposable fixtures:
the FDU-089 loopback credential and a deliberately incomplete JWT used to prove
rejection. A new match blocks publication and requires rotation when authenticity
cannot be disproved. Never put a finding's secret value in evidence.

The 2026-10-18 inventory found 1,726 tracked files, 610 scanned commits, one human
contributor identity  two author-name spellings with the same email , and four
retained manual build artifacts. The GitHub repository was private and  main  had
no branch-protection rule. Before visibility changes, enable private vulnerability
reporting, publish SECURITY and contribution policies, protect  main , confirm
release artifacts contain only intended packages, and rerun both commands.

Repository history contains public project/source links, example.invalid-style
fixtures and the operational hostname  update.fedrv.de . No customer identity or
private service address was found. Production configuration and credentials stay
outside Git. Historical task evidence is public engineering provenance and must
be reviewed as such; accepted records are immutable.

   Publication decision checklist

1. Owner approves the exact license recorded in  license-decision.md .
2. All FDU-158 audit findings are closed and all D008 documentation/security
   policies are present.
3. The D008 gate and independent review accept one exact commit.
4. Owner explicitly authorizes GitHub visibility change. Capture the repository
   ID, source commit, settings baseline and timestamp before changing visibility.
5. Set visibility once, verify anonymous clone/docs/license/security links, then
   retain the prior settings record for rollback. A visibility rollback cannot
   retract already downloaded history, so a secret finding always requires
   rotation rather than relying on making the repository private again.

title: Installation Accounts
text:
Installation Accounts

Installation Accounts are human download and delegated-enrollment identities.
They are separate from administrator accounts, repository publishing credentials
and the Ed25519 identity/credential generated for each installed software
instance.

The durable account domain is owned by  fdupdate-installation-accounts . IDs use
UTC  YYMMDDNN , where  NN  is the first unused sequence from  00  through  99 
for that date. A day cannot create a 101st account; it fails explicitly instead
of changing the identifier shape or reusing an ID.

Email login is normalized to trimmed lowercase ASCII and must be unique. The
server generates a 192-bit initial password, returns it once, stores an Argon2id
verifier and requires a password change. Account views, audit and  Debug  never
contain password material. A positive installation limit is exact;  None  means
unlimited. Repository grants contain only canonical exact project keys and do
not derive authority from product or component names.

   Owner administration

The authenticated  /admin  page contains a separate   Installation Accounts  
section. Owner authority and a current CSRF value are required to create an
account, change its exact private-repository grants or installation limit,
enable or disable it, and reset its password. Public and unknown repositories
are rejected as grants. A limit is either one positive integer or explicitly
unlimited.

Creation and reset return a  no-store  page containing the Installation ID and
generated password once. Later dashboards show only safe account metadata and
bounded audit. Reset invalidates the prior password immediately; disablement
prevents authentication immediately. Future Installation Account sessions and
download or enrollment requests must re-read current enabled state and grants
rather than treating their initial session projection as durable authority.

Deployment stores  installation-accounts.json  beside the other mutable web
runtime state under the service-writable web data directory. It is not placed in
the root-owned secret directory, and that directory remains read-only to the web
service.

   Confirmation and self-service

The owner configures one FDUpdate-private Email channel through COT. Its
protected setup binds the sender account and SMTP provider configuration, while
each message supplies exactly one validated Installation Account recipient.
SMTP credentials pass directly from the protected owner form into COT custody;
FDUpdate retains only the opaque channel identity and revision. FDUpdate never
persists SMTP credentials or a recipient-specific COT resource.

New accounts remain unusable until their current email is confirmed. The
Installation Account portal supports login by ID or normalized email, forced
initial password change, password recovery and confirmed email replacement.
Confirmation and recovery links are short-lived, single-use and replaced by a
newer challenge of the same kind. Only a SHA-256 digest of each random token is
stored. Passwords are never sent by email. Password recovery, email replacement,
owner reset, authority changes and disablement revoke existing Installation
Account sessions.

The dynamic-recipient contract uses the typed COT SDK published at revision
 9f720a6ed5a68dd1fa5df5716fdf7bea57e67c0e  and an isolated conforming fixture.
The same immutable COT candidate is deployed on the authorized VPS and its live
health probe passes. FDUpdate treats compatibility as verified only when the
typed fixture, security, UI, deployment and redaction checks all pass against
that exact pin; the upstream task's unrelated open lifecycle state is not a
runtime compatibility signal.

Delegated software enrollment uses the account password only as transient proof.
The account's current grants must cover the installation's exact requested
repository set, and its optional installation limit counts distinct signed
software identities. Exact retries are idempotent; successful software receives
an independent installation credential. The human password is never persisted
in updater or registry state.

Registration audit idempotency is bound to a domain-separated semantic attempt:
the digest of the signed enrollment request, tenant/product/component scope,
provenance, resolved Installation Account ID when available, software instance
and exact sorted repository set. Occurrence time and outcome do not change that
attempt identity; outcome remains a separate audit transition key. Consequently
an exact retry produces no duplicate row, while two repository/provenance/account
variations remain distinct durable attempts even when they reuse one signed
software identity. Audit schema v1 records migrate deterministically to v2 from
their stored request digest and redacted semantic fields. Passwords, email,
request bodies, installation credentials and signed decisions are neither inputs
persisted in the audit nor exposed by its query.

   Private download portal

After the required password change,  /installation-account  projects only the
account's current exact grants that are still private. Each published release
lists its digest-bound artifacts. Downloads use authenticated
 /installation-account/downloads/{project}/{release}/{sha256}  routes, support
HTTP ranges, verify the stored bytes against the published digest and return a
concealed 404 for public, unknown, ungranted or mismatched targets. The account
session grants no administrator or publication authority.

An account can create a bearer link for one listed artifact for 1 through 30
days; the form defaults to 10 days. The plaintext HTTPS URL is shown once, while
the portal inventory keeps only its non-secret grant ID, exact target, expiry
and status. The same link can download the same verified bytes repeatedly until
expiry or account revocation. Its owner can revoke it from the portal with the
current session and CSRF token.

Every account-created link is additionally bound to its Installation Account.
Redemption re-reads the current enabled account, confirmed email and exact
repository grants. Removing the grant, disabling the account, losing current
email confirmation, expiry, explicit revocation, or any public/private
visibility transition invalidates the link immediately. A later transition
back to private does not resurrect it. Other accounts cannot list or revoke the
grant, even when they share repository access.

title: Installation dashboard
text:
Installation dashboard

Authenticated owners, fleet operators and security administrators open  /admin/installations  from the administration page. The dashboard only requests products backed by repositories visible to the signed-in account. Application rows carrying repository provenance are filtered again against those repository scopes.

Each installation has one card keyed by its unique instance ID. The card shows enrollment state, fingerprint, source installation-key ID, repository grants and the last server contact. Contact within 15 minutes is labelled online; older contact is labelled offline/stale; an absent timestamp is labelled never seen. These labels describe any authenticated device contact rather than device attestation.

The separate managed-updater status comes from its heartbeat. The panel displays updater version plus client-reported and server-received heartbeat times. A heartbeat received within 15 minutes is online, an older heartbeat is offline/stale, no heartbeat is never reported, and a non-approved enrollment is inactive. Liveness uses the server-received time, so a client cannot keep itself online by supplying a future clock value. A stale updater does not by itself mean that an application update failed.

Each configured application binding is visible before its first application report. Its row identifies the target, repository, platform, architecture, channel, check permission, update permission and binding revision. The last-check column keeps the client-reported and server-received check times distinct. A binding without a report shows  never reported , an unknown health and no assignment.

Reported rows show the client-reported installed version, assigned version and assignment ID, local Release/Prerelease channel, last update health/error, last check and last successful update. Publication or assignment never fills the installed-version column. Historical reported state without a current binding is retained as  not currently managed  rather than being presented as active authority.

Changing a binding's repository, platform, architecture or channel starts a new current outcome epoch. The first report still shows its installed version and check times, but it remains  unknown  until that exact provenance reports an outcome; health, last-success time and diagnostics from the previous provenance stay only in bounded history and are never relabelled into another repository scope.

The  q  filter matches installation ID, fingerprint, enrollment state, installation key, repository, product/component, installed and updater versions, platform, architecture, channel, managed permissions, health, errors and heartbeat/check times. Results can be sorted by last contact, installation ID or enrollment state and are paged at 25 installations. Approval, revocation and grant management links return to the existing CSRF-protected controls.

The layout uses a full table at desktop width and labelled stacked cells below 600 px. All client strings are escaped before rendering, responses use  Cache-Control: no-store , query input is bounded to 128 bytes and page numbers are bounded.

title: Migrating FDOS to external FDUpdater
text:
Migrating FDOS to external FDUpdater

 FDUpdaterFdosMigration  converts the strict FDOS updater v1 configuration,
current/previous slot metadata and idle engine state into a separate FDUpdater
state root. It never edits or removes the FDOS root and never changes a service.

Create an administrator-owned request outside both roots:

   json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "legacy_config": "ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_FDOS_UPDATER_CONFIG",
  "state_root": "ABSOLUTE_NEW_FDUPDATER_STATE_ROOT",
  "instance_id": "fdos-installation-1",
  "architecture": "x86_64",
  "updater_identity": "FDUpdater.service",
  "application_identity": "FDOS.application"
}
   

Stop FDOS_Updater, then run the explicit migration:

   text
FDUpdaterFdosMigration migrate --request ABSOLUTE_REQUEST_JSON
   

The destination must not exist. The command opens and exclusively locks the
existing  updater.lock ; a running updater or a missing lock file blocks migration
without creating or modifying legacy state. The command also rejects an active transaction,
unknown fields or schemas, unsupported components/platforms, inconsistent
configuration, invalid trust material and any slot whose executable does not
match its size and SHA-256. It builds the complete destination in a sibling
temporary directory and publishes it with one non-overwriting atomic move. A
rejected or interrupted migration therefore leaves both the requested destination
absent and FDOS_Updater unchanged.

The package contains:

-  fdupdater-registry.json  with explicit  fdos/server ,  fdos/agent  and, when
  configured,  fdos/updater  registrations using the original service names;
- copied immutable current and previous executables plus their converted slot
  metadata and retained FDOS artifact-signature domain;
- one  transaction.json  per target with the legacy replay cursor and failed
  sequence, but no active transaction;
-  fdos-trust.json  containing only the legacy public verification keys;
-  fdos-compat.json  retaining polling, CA, pause and local health-command policy;
-  fdos-migration.json , a deterministic receipt bound to the source config/state
  hashes and migrated versions.

Application data remains at its existing path. Keep the complete legacy root and
FDOS_Updater service definition until FDUpdater health and rollback have been
verified by the deployment procedure. Service activation belongs to the installer
and is deliberately outside the conversion command.

The later FDOS repository change should remove the in-process/workspace
 fdos-updater  dependency and stop publishing application-owned updater commands.
Its installer should provision FDUpdater independently, run this migration once,
then switch the existing FDOS Server and Agent service ownership only after the
migration receipt and FDUpdater health pass. FDOS UI actions should call the
authenticated local FDUpdater API for status, check, apply, rollback, pause,
resume and diagnostics using the  fdos  product and existing component names.
If release publication temporarily keeps the strict FDOS v1 envelope, its
compatibility provider must verify the retained original bytes in the distinct
FDOS signature domain before giving normalized metadata to FDUpdater. The local
state migration does not authenticate or authorize a new remote release. After
rollout validation, FDOS can publish the product-neutral FDUpdate envelope and
remove the legacy adapter in a separately versioned migration. The rollback
procedure restores the original service definitions and legacy root without
converting state back or deleting the FDUpdater package.

title: FDUpdater native packages
text:
FDUpdater native packages

FDUpdater packages are built offline from the two release binaries and checked-in
installer sources. The builder writes deterministic  .tar.gz  for Linux and  .zip 
for Windows. Every payload has a strict manifest and SHA-256 inventory. Packages
contain no credential, private key, product registration, application data or
pre-authorized target.

Build the native binaries and one package from the repository root:

   text
cargo +1.98.0 build --release --locked -p fdupdater -p fdupdater-bootstrap
node scripts/package-fdupdater.mjs --platform windows --architecture x86_64 --version 0.1.0 --fdupdater target/release/FDUpdater.exe --bootstrap target/release/FDUpdaterBootstrap.exe --output dist
   

Use  --platform linux  and extensionless binary paths on Linux. Building identical
inputs twice produces byte-identical archives on the same platform. Release
publication must authenticate the archive separately; the embedded hashes detect
damage but are not a release signature.

After extraction, run the installer from an elevated PowerShell on Windows:

   text
./install.ps1 install
./install.ps1 status
./install.ps1 upgrade
./install.ps1 repair
./install.ps1 uninstall
   

Run the corresponding commands as root on a systemd Linux host:

   text
./install.sh install
./install.sh status
./install.sh upgrade
./install.sh repair
./install.sh uninstall
   

Installation creates the automatic  FDUpdater  service under the virtual Windows
service identity  NT SERVICE\FDUpdater  or the non-root Linux account  fdupdater .
The binary directory is administrator-owned and read-only to the service. Only the
state directory is service-writable. The configuration directory is readable by
the service and contains a placeholder-only template. Before  install , an
administrator must create the strict  FDUpdater.json , credentials, public trust
and product registrations described in
 runtime-operations.md  runtime-operations.md . Installation fails closed when
that production configuration is absent and passes its absolute path to systemd
or SCM.

Upgrade stages and self-tests both binaries before stopping the service. Failure
restores the prior current/previous layout and attempts to restart the prior
service. Repair replaces owned binaries and service policy without changing state
or configuration. Uninstall deletes the service definition and binary root while
retaining configuration, state and recovery data. Application roots are never an
installer argument and are never traversed. Removing retained state is a separate
administrator action outside the package command.

The documented native acceptance command is the manual-only GitHub workflow
 FDUpdater native package acceptance    workflow_dispatch  . Its Linux and Windows
jobs build each archive twice and generate ephemeral signing material outside the
package. They install into unique native roots, apply a signed release through the
installed CLI, force and recover an interrupted transaction, verify boot-style
restart, corrupt and repair the owned updater binary, upgrade it, uninstall it,
and compare state, recovery and external application-data canaries. No fixture
private key enters either package. The same scenarios can be run from a repository
checkout on clean hosts with:

   text
cargo +1.98.0 build --release --locked -p fdupdater --example native_fixture
sudo bash packaging/linux/native-acceptance.sh ABSOLUTE_EXPANDED_PACKAGE_ROOT "$PWD/target/release/examples/native_fixture"
powershell -File packaging/windows/native-acceptance.ps1 -PackageRoot ABSOLUTE_EXPANDED_PACKAGE_ROOT -FixtureTool "$PWD/target/release/examples/native_fixture.exe"
