title: Public update catalog
text:
Public update catalog

 fdupdate-web  serves an anonymous catalog from the canonical repository registry and publisher provenance journal. Its configuration supplies a bare HTTPS  public_origin , private bind address, repository/publisher state files and immutable artifact store. The process binds only to loopback or a private edge address; the deployment edge owns public TLS.

The index and repository pages include only repositories marked  public . Each version shows release ID, publication time, publisher, GitHub repository, exact source commit and escaped publication comment. Every artifact has a direct link, a read-only link field and a copy button. The link remains a normal anchor when scripting is unavailable.

Private and unknown project keys use the same  404 Not found  response for repository and download routes. A download succeeds only when the project is currently public, its provenance record names the exact release and digest, every store path component is a real directory, the artifact is a bounded regular non-symlink file, and its bytes hash to the requested SHA-256. The already-open verified file is streamed with  application/octet-stream  and  nosniff . Catalog, manifest and artifact responses use  Cache-Control: no-store  because repository visibility can change; previously distributed bytes and legacy cache entries cannot be recalled.

Artifact responses advertise  Accept-Ranges: bytes . A single bounded byte range
returns  206 Partial Content  only after the complete stored file has passed its
provenance, size and SHA-256 checks. Open-ended and suffix ranges support restart
and resume; malformed, multiple or unsatisfiable ranges return  416  with the
verified complete size. The same behavior applies to authenticated private and
temporary-link downloads without weakening their authorization or cache policy.

Public repositories also expose  /latest-manifests/PROJECT_KEY  for polling clients. It resolves the newest accepted publication on every request, reopens the provenance-bound signed manifest and uses  no-store ; signature verification and the FDUpdater sequence cursor reject forged or replayed releases. Exact  /manifests/PROJECT_KEY/RELEASE_ID  URLs remain immutable.

An administrator may separately issue a secret temporary bearer URL for one exact artifact in a private repository. Its selected lifetime is 1 through 30 days and defaults to 10 days. This does not make the repository or its manifest public: the  /share/<token>  route knows only the persisted exact target, revalidates current private visibility and returns verified immutable bytes on repeated requests until expiry. Unknown, expired and no-longer-private targets use the same not-found response. The edge does not write share-token paths to its access log. Legacy single-use grant records remain readable and retain consume-before-stream behavior.

Local verification:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdate-web --all-targets --locked
cargo clippy -p fdupdate-web --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

title: Release inventory panel
text:
Release inventory panel

The authenticated  /admin/releases  route renders the live repository registry and retention catalog through  fdupdate-server-panel . The page includes active and revoked repositories without copying workflow identity, credentials, signing keys or artifact content into the response. The main  /admin  dashboard links to this page.

The standalone panel API retains its scoped  OperatorService  authorization contract. The production HTTP route requires the administrator session on every read and requires the matching session CSRF token for mutations. A valid change is written atomically with actor, request, time, previous values and new values in the retention catalog. Invalid, sessionless and CSRF-invalid requests preserve the prior settings.

The page reports each version's target, channel, status, manifest digest, artifact bytes, publication and cleanup time and protection reason. Repository and server totals distinguish retained, pinned, reclaimable and cleaned data. Empty repositories remain visible. A stale snapshot carries its capture time and reason. An unavailable snapshot suppresses all partial inventory and totals and displays the failure explicitly.

The HTML includes a viewport declaration, horizontally scrollable wide inventory tables and a compact layout below 600 CSS pixels. The web runtime reads the catalog for every request. A missing or invalid catalog produces an explicit unavailable page without partial totals; an old catalog modification time produces a stale banner with its timestamp.

title: Manual release publication
text:
Manual release publication

 fdupdate-publisher  is the short-lived offline publication boundary. It consumes canonical  fdupdate/publication-plan/v1  JSON plus  fdupdate/build-evidence/v1  records, verifies each bounded artifact byte-for-byte, signs artifact metadata and the canonical release manifest, stages an invisible hawkBit distribution, and atomically installs immutable content before activation.

The caller supplies a  SigningAuthority  only for one explicit operator or manual  workflow_dispatch  operation. The authority cannot be formatted or serialized. Stored artifacts, evidence, receipts, backend tokens and errors contain no private key material. Runtime server and updater components do not depend on this crate.

 PublicationBackend  is the private hawkBit transaction adapter.  prepare  must create an invisible distribution,  commit  makes it deployable, and  abort  is idempotent. Failed evidence is rejected before preparation. Failed activation removes the newly staged immutable directory and aborts the upstream transaction while preserving all earlier releases.

Focused verification:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdate-publisher --test publication --locked
cargo clippy -p fdupdate-publisher --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

title: Release retention
text:
Release retention

 fdupdate-retention  stores the server-wide stable and prerelease retention policy and the release cleanup journal in one atomically replaced JSON catalog. Both channel limits default to 10 and accept values from 1 through 1000.

Retention is evaluated independently for each publisher, product, component, platform and architecture. The immutable server publication time orders releases within each stable or prerelease channel. Assignment, rollout, validation-stand, rollback-window and recovery-window pins keep an otherwise expired release and are reported by the cleanup result.

Cleanup first persists the selected release as unavailable with  cleanup_pending . It then asks the artifact backend to make the complete release unavailable and confirm that all release-owned bytes are absent. A confirmed cleanup is finalized with an immutable tombstone containing cleanup time and reason plus the manifest and artifact digests and sizes. If deletion or final persistence fails, the pending record remains unavailable and the next run retries safely. Completed tombstones are excluded from later runs.

The backend implementation must make  remove_release  idempotent and must remove a release as one logical unit. Operators should inspect reported pins and tombstones through the inventory panel before changing recovery policy.

   Running server worker

The GitHub publisher gateway owns cleanup transitions. Every accepted repository publication is added to  retention-catalog.json  before the API returns, then a worker runs at startup, after publication and every configured interval. The authenticated web panel may update only the two retention counts. Both processes serialize catalog mutations with the catalog lock and reject stale writes; cleanup holds the lock through its backend deletion and journal transitions. Deployment values seed a new catalog and never overwrite a later web-panel choice after restart. The deployed defaults are 10 stable versions, 10 prerelease versions, a batch of 10 cleanup candidates and a 3600-second interval. Missed timer ticks are skipped, so runs never overlap.  GET /retention/status  on the private publisher address reports only run, failure, removal and byte counters; it never returns hawkBit credentials or repository secrets.

Before each run the worker reads the durable device-gateway state and refreshes  active_assignment ,  rollback_window  and  recovery_window  pins. Missing or invalid device state aborts that run without changing availability. A failed cleanup remains  cleanup_pending  and is retried on the next run or process restart.

Each new publication durably records its repository-scoped hawkBit distribution-set and software-module IDs before publication commit. Cleanup first commits  available=false  to the catalog. Web and device delivery reopen that catalog before opening release bytes, so requests begun after the transition fail closed. The worker then deletes the private hawkBit objects, atomically moves the repository release directory out of  releases , removes its bytes and records the tombstone. DELETE accepts hawkBit  404  as an idempotent retry result, is limited to ten seconds per request, and never derives a path outside  repositories/<project>/releases/<release> .

At startup the publisher reconciles its immutable publication journal with storage. Releases created before the hawkBit cleanup journal existed receive an explicit  recovery_window  pin. They remain downloadable and visible but are never automatically reclaimed because their upstream identity cannot be proven. Operators must migrate or retire those releases through a separately accepted recovery procedure rather than deleting the pin manually.

title: Repository administration
text:
Repository administration

The private area of  fdupdate-web  is available under  /admin . Administrator
identity is an individual canonical account ID. The durable account document
stores enabled/owner state, revisioned audit records and only a domain-separated
SHA-256 credential verifier. It never stores plaintext credentials. Set
 admin_account_state_file  to a protected state path; when omitted, it defaults
to  administrator-accounts.json  beside  admin_credential_file .

On the first start without an account document, the runtime reads the existing
high-entropy  admin_credential_file  and migrates it to one enabled bootstrap
owner named by  admin_actor_id . The migration commits atomically before login is
available, so an existing installation keeps access. Later starts use the account
document and no longer require the legacy credential file. Do not delete the
legacy file until one successful migrated start and protected-state backup have
been confirmed.

Account state schema v2 adds an ordered role set and explicit repository scopes.
Opening a valid v1 document migrates it atomically: existing owners keep their
owner capability and non-owner accounts remain enabled with  Reader  and no
repository scope, which grants no repository access. A failed migration preserves
the last valid document; restore that protected file or use  recover-owner  if no
owner credential remains usable.

An owner can create an account, disable an account or rotate its credential from
the panel. New and rotated 256-bit credentials appear on one non-cacheable page
only. Duplicate or malformed IDs fail closed, writes use revision checks and an
atomic replacement, and the last enabled owner cannot be disabled. Every account
mutation records the acting and subject account IDs without a credential. Other
administrative audit records use the account ID from the authenticated session.

Owners assign access from each account card. Repository scopes are canonical
project keys separated by commas. They must already exist and match exactly;
empty scope means no repository access. The runtime reloads current authorization
for every request, so role removal, scope removal and owner removal affect active
sessions immediately. The account audit records the actor, subject, resulting
owner flag, roles and scopes.

The web authorization matrix is:

| Capability | Required access |
| --- | --- |
| Accounts, repository creation, retention and server update | Owner |
| Inventory, repository metadata and authenticated download | Any assigned role plus the exact repository scope |
| Publishing-key rotation and revocation |  ReleaseManager  plus the exact repository scope |
| Product-wide installation approval, denial and identity revocation |  SecurityAdministrator  covering every repository for the product, or owner |
| Exact repository admission, visibility and temporary shares |  SecurityAdministrator  plus the exact repository scope |
| Enrollment codes |  SecurityAdministrator  covering every repository matching the product/component, or owner |
| Fleet status | Read-only  FleetOperator  or  SecurityAdministrator  plus the exact repository scope |

Owners bypass repository role and scope checks. Submitted project, product and
component IDs are resolved against the durable registry before a backend request.
Product-wide installation mutations require complete product coverage, and an
enrollment code requires complete coverage of the selected product/component.
Fleet status includes an installation when at least one repository for its
product is in scope, filters repository-grant names to those exact scopes, and
renders mutation controls only when the corresponding security authority is
complete. Role and scope changes affect that projection on the next request.
The repository adapter also filters reads and rejects mutations outside its
received scopes, so hiding a control in the page is never the authorization
boundary. Unknown, malformed and guessed identifiers fail closed.

A successful login creates a random 256-bit session and independent CSRF token.
The browser cookie is  HttpOnly ,  Secure ,  SameSite=Strict , restricted to
 /admin  and bounded by the configured 5-minute to 24-hour lifetime. Account
enabled state is checked again on each request, so disabling an account rejects
its existing cookies immediately. Current roles and scopes are checked at the
same boundary. Sessions are intentionally lost on service restart.

The   Administrator sessions   panel lists only a random non-authorizing session
reference, account, server-observed TCP client address and creation/expiry times.
It never displays the cookie verifier or CSRF value. Every administrator can log
out, revoke one of their sessions or revoke all of their sessions. An owner can
inspect and revoke sessions for every account. A single-session revoke preserves
unrelated sessions. Disabling an account or rotating its credential revokes all
of that account's sessions immediately; host-local owner recovery is performed
while the service is stopped, and restart discards every prior session.

Authentication settings are stored atomically in
 administrator-auth-settings.json  beside the account document unless
 admin_auth_settings_state_file  selects another protected path. On the first
start, the existing  session_ttl_seconds  value initializes this document. Later
starts use the persisted document. Owners can configure these bounded values:

| Setting | Allowed range | Initial value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session lifetime | 300–86,400 seconds | Existing  session_ttl_seconds  |
| Failed logins before cooldown | 3–20 | 5 |
| Failure window | 60–3,600 seconds | 300 seconds |
| Cooldown | 30–3,600 seconds | 300 seconds |

Every change records the owner account and complete resulting non-secret settings.
Shortening the session lifetime also shortens existing sessions immediately;
increasing it applies to new sessions and does not extend cookies already issued.
Invalid, stale, corrupt and non-owner changes fail closed while preserving the
last valid file.

Login throttling is memory-bounded and keyed only by the web process's actual TCP
peer address. User-supplied  Forwarded ,  X-Forwarded-For  and  X-Real-IP  headers
are ignored. The supported edge removes those headers and applies its own stricter
 /admin/login  rate limit before proxying. With the standard single edge, the
application-level bucket is intentionally shared by traffic arriving from that
edge; this is conservative and prevents forged client headers from creating new
buckets. Restart clears in-memory failure counters while retaining the configured
limits.

If all usable credentials are lost, stop  fdupdate-web  and run the host-local
recovery command with access to the protected configuration and state directory:

   text
fdupdate-web recover-owner CONFIG.json ACCOUNT_ID
   

The command enables or creates the named owner, rotates its verifier, records a
 local-recovery  audit event and prints the new credential once. Start the service
again after securing that value. Running recovery while the service is accepting
traffic is unsupported; revision checks reject a stale subsequent writer rather
than overwrite the recovered state.

Every administrator page and response uses  Cache-Control: no-store . Every mutation requires the current session and exact constant-time CSRF match. Request bodies are capped at 64 KiB. Administrator credentials, session tokens, CSRF tokens and publishing credentials are absent from repository audit and logs.

When the optional server-updater integration is configured,  /admin  also shows the exact managed FDUpdate Server target: current and previous versions, pending release, health and recovery.   Check for server updates   refreshes provider state.   Install server update   is shown only for a pending candidate and

title: FDUpdater runtime operations
text:
FDUpdater runtime operations

The installed service reads one administrator-owned  FDUpdater.json . Linux starts
it as  FDUpdater service --name NAME --config /absolute/FDUpdater.json ; Windows
registers the equivalent SCM image path. Startup rejects an absent file, unknown
JSON fields, relative or aliased paths, non-loopback API addresses, overlapping
target/state roots, unreadable credentials and trust, or an unsafe provider
endpoint. The service recovers every durable transaction before accepting API
mutations.

Start from  packaging/common/FDUpdater.example.json  and provision the completed
file before install. The reader and operator credential files must be distinct.
Give the service read access to configuration, public trust, provider metadata and
artifacts; give it write access only to its state root and registered application
installation roots. Signing private keys never belong on the device.

 poll_interval_seconds  controls the normal remote-work cadence. The optional
 retry  block sets the initial and maximum retry delay and the maximum
deterministic jitter. Repeated distribution, enrollment or application transport
failure persists an exponential retry deadline in the state root, so restart does
not create a request burst. A successful remote cycle clears the retry streak.
Watchdog supervision continues on the normal cadence while remote work backs off.

 provider.kind  is  manifest ,  remote_manifest ,  gateway  or  hawkbit . A manifest provider
reads a locally administered signed envelope and resolves its artifact only as
 ARTIFACT_ROOT/SHA256.artifact . A remote-manifest provider reads a public HTTPS
signed-release URL, either an exact immutable release or a  no-store  latest-publication
endpoint, and downloads only the artifact URL covered by that signature. It disables redirects and proxies, bounds metadata and
artifact bytes, verifies TLS, signature, size and SHA-256, and optionally accepts
one administrator-provisioned PEM root certificate. A hawkBit provider requires an HTTPS base URL,
tenant, controller ID and a separate target-token file; an optional PEM root file
pins a private deployment CA. Both providers produce the same signed-release
contract, and product trust still authorizes every artifact.

A gateway provider points  endpoint  at the product-scoped application route,
for example  https://update.example/v1/application/default/fdos/ . Every
standalone target using this provider also configures its product-scoped
 enrollment.endpoint . FDUpdater creates and protects the installation key under
 state_root , polls enrollment until an administrator approves it, and uses the
returned per-installation credential for check, package and report requests. The
server-side repository grant selects which repository may supply the release;
the client stores no publisher key, administrator session or share credential.

The gateway endpoint must use HTTPS, contain no credentials, query or fragment,
and end with  / . Redirects are rejected.  root_certificate_file  may pin a
private deployment CA. Package responses are streamed with the signed size bound
and then pass the normal signature, digest, compatibility, channel, readiness and
rollback pipeline. A pending gateway assignment stores its local target so
restart recovery can reacquire only that installation's current credential and
report the final result.

Each  targets  entry fixes the product/component instance, platform, architecture,
installation root, executable name, service binding, health policy, data roots and
initial version. Lifecycle commands and paths come only from this local entry.
Set  manual_apply  to  true  for a target whose releases may be discovered by the
normal polling cycle but may be activated only by an authenticated explicit
 apply  action. The field defaults to  false  for compatibility, so existing
targets retain automatic activation.
Optional enrollment, readiness, watchdog and diagnostics blocks use separate
credentials and loopback endpoints where applicable. An application-managed
target also requires enrollment and the root  application_updates  HTTPS endpoint.

Use the packaged binary and a provisioned credential to inspect or control the
runtime:

   text
FDUpdater status --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file READER
FDUpdater check --instance INSTANCE --product PRODUCT --component COMPONENT --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file READER
FDUpdater apply --instance INSTANCE --product PRODUCT --component COMPONENT --expected-sequence SEQUENCE --expected-version VERSION --expected-action-id ACTION_ID --expected-release-sha256 RELEASE_SHA256 --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file OPERATOR
FDUpdater pause --instance INSTANCE --product PRODUCT --component COMPONENT --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file OPERATOR
FDUpdater resume --instance INSTANCE --product PRODUCT --component COMPONENT --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file OPERATOR
FDUpdater diagnostics --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file READER
FDUpdater enrollment --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file READER
FDUpdater app-updates --endpoint 127.0.0.1:17483 --credential-file READER
   

Before  apply , read  pending_rollout  from the target returned by  check  or
 status . Pass its  sequence ,  version ,  action_id  and  release_sha256  as the
four  --expected-   values above. FDUpdater compares that complete identity with
the currently pending signed release inside the serialized Apply operation. If
polling replaced the release, it is no longer pending, or any value differs,
Apply returns a conflict without downloading or activating another candidate;
run  check  again and review the new identity before retrying.

 status  reports durable current/previous versions, pending rollout, channel,
recovery state, watchdog state and incident summary. Provider or network failure
leaves the current slot intact. Verification, enrollment, readiness, lifecycle or
health failure denies completion and drives deterministic rollback. Restarting the
service repeats startup recovery before polling. Windows SCM stop and Linux
SIGINT/SIGTERM immediately cancel the shared lifecycle token and reject new API
mutations. An in-flight transition stops at its next durable cancellation boundary
and remains in a recoverable phase; the next service start completes recovery
before polling or accepting mutations.

title: Server flow for application-managed updates
text:
Server flow for application-managed updates

The server creates a bounded assignment for one approved installation, exact product/component, channel, version and signed release. Check requests first authenticate the installation against the registry, then match that exact assignment. Paused assignments and other channels return no offer; revoked identities fail authentication. Artifact delivery continues through the approval and replay gate.

Progress and final reports authenticate against the same assignment. An identical retry is accepted without a second audit event; a changed report for the same assignment conflicts. The audit supplies the installation, assignment, outcome and installed version to rollout policy. Rollback releases use the signed rollback authorization already embedded in the assigned release.

title: Metadata and artifact delivery authorization
text:
Metadata and artifact delivery authorization

The TLS server evaluates every metadata and artifact request before reading or returning a payload. It authenticates the per-installation credential against the approved public-key enrollment, verifies tenant/product/component scope, confirms the installation belongs to the selected rollout cohort, and consumes a bounded request ID to reject replay.

Anonymous, pending, denied, revoked, wrong-product, wrong-component and unassigned callers receive neither metadata nor artifact bytes. Revocation is checked before replay state changes. Tenant-wide hawkBit credentials stay inside the server adapter; clients receive only signed release metadata and their own installation credential.

   Repository grants

Approval and repository access are separate decisions. A newly enrolled or newly
approved installation starts with no individual repository grant. The effective
set is the union of individual grants and the current allowlist of the installation
key that admitted it. The operator API changes individual grants with authenticated
requests to:

-  POST /v1/operator/repositories/grant 
-  POST /v1/operator/repositories/revoke 

Both accept  tenant ,  product_id ,  instance_id , and the repository
 project_key . The grant operation requires an approved installation. A revoked
grant takes effect on checks, package downloads, digest downloads, and reports,
including assignments created before the revocation.

Changing an installation key allowlist takes effect at the next metadata,
package, digest, or report authorization check. Removing a repository therefore
removes inherited access without rewriting every installation. Disabling a key
controls only new admission.  updates_suspended  is a separate audited policy:
while set, all existing installations admitted by that key lose its inherited
grants, but keep any explicit individual grants. Clearing the suspension restores
the then-current key allowlist. Revoking one installation credential remains
independent of all other installations that used the same key.

The device gateway searches only
 store/repositories/<project_key>/releases . It validates the signed manifest,
matches the requested product, component, platform and architecture, filters the
requested channel, and then compares semantic versions. The Release channel
excludes prerelease versions. The Prerelease channel considers both stable and
prerelease versions using normal SemVer ordering. Each assignment identity binds
the installation, repository, exact product/component target, artifact digest,
complete signed-release envelope and exact Release or Prerelease policy through a
length-framed, domain-separated SHA-256 derivation. A later signed version,
sequence or channel receives its own identity even when it deliberately reuses the
same immutable artifact bytes. The resulting opaque  a-  identifier fits the
shared standalone action-ID limit; persisted identifiers from both previous
opaque derivations and the two earlier digest-suffix formats remain resolvable
only for their exact stored assignment and channel.
It persists the repository key that supplied it, and every later package or digest lookup repeats
the current grant check before opening that repository namespace.

The standalone client persists the exact local target selected by the successful
gateway check. Eligibility, status, download, activation, restart reconciliation
and outcome reporting all use that target. Other locally registered components,
including components whose signed artifacts contain identical bytes, require
their own check and assignment before they can change.

Repository grants are stored atomically with the installation registry. Older
registry snapshots deserialize with an empty grant set, so migration does not
authorize repositories based on matching product, component, or version. Older
assignments have no repository provenance and cannot serve artifact bytes; the
installation must check again after an explicit grant to receive a new assignment.

   Managed application bindings

Repository access alone does not authorize a managed updater to check or update an application. An operator must also create a revisioned binding through  POST /v1/operator/managed-applications/bind . The request fixes one updater instance to an exact component, repository, platform, architecture and Release/Prerelease channel and sets  check_allowed  and  update_allowed  independently.  update_allowed  requires check access.  expected_revision  is zero for the first binding and must match the current revision for every reconciliation.

 POST /v1/operator/managed-applications/unbind  disables both permissions and advances the revision without losing the replay barrier. The gateway rechecks the current binding before assignment creation, package or digest delivery and outcome reporting. A channel change invalidates earlier-channel delivery immediately; a check-only binding records honest inventory and returns no assignment. These operator routes require the private gateway operator token and persist by atomic state replacement.

title: FDUpdate Server foundation deployment
text:
FDUpdate Server foundation deployment

FDU-017 provides the first supported server foundation: one  linux/amd64  host,
Docker Engine with the Compose v2 plugin, Eclipse hawkBit 1.1.0, MariaDB 11.4 and
an nginx TLS/mTLS edge. All three images are pinned by immutable registry digest.
Only the edge publishes a host port. hawkBit, its Management API, MariaDB and the
artifact directory remain private.

The foundation is deliberately sealed.  /healthz  is the only anonymous route.
 /operator-ready  returns 204 only with a client certificate signed by the
configured operator CA. Every other route returns 401 until the FDUpdate gateway
implemented by later Epic 002 tasks owns device and operator authorization. Do not
publish hawkBit directly.

   Trusted public TLS

After public DNS points at the host and inbound TCP 80/443 is allowed, expose the
edge with a trusted ACME certificate through the deployment CLI:

   bash
sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server public-tls \
  --install-root /opt/fdupdate-server \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --data-root /var/lib/fdupdate-server \
  --server-name update.example.com \
  --acme-email operations@example.com
   

The command obtains an ECDSA certificate with Certbot's standalone HTTP-01
listener, changes only the edge binding to  0.0.0.0:443 , recreates the edge and
installs a renewal deploy hook. The hook atomically copies renewed transport
material and recreates the edge; hawkBit and MariaDB remain unpublished. Omitting
 --acme-email  uses Certbot's explicit no-email registration mode.

   Host prerequisites

- A dedicated x86-64 Linux host with a current Docker Engine and Compose v2.
-  bash , GNU coreutils,  curl  and OpenSSL.
- Root access for configuration creation and lifecycle changes.
- Host firewall policy for the selected listener. The generated configuration
  binds  127.0.0.1:8443 ; changing it to  0.0.0.0  is an explicit operator action.

Executable releases, configuration and durable data use separate roots:

   text
/opt/fdupdate-server          versioned compose/nginx releases and current/previous links
/etc/fdupdate-server          deployment.env, runtime secrets and TLS/mTLS material
/var/lib/fdupdate-server      MariaDB and immutable artifact bytes
   

Release-signing keys never belong in any of these runtime containers. The TLS and
operator CA keys created below are transport identity material. They remain in the
root-only host configuration directory and are not mounted into containers except
for the server TLS key itself; replace the acceptance PKI under your operational
CA before exposing a production listener.

   Clean install

From an exact repository checkout, create the private configuration and validate
the candidate before starting containers:

   bash
sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server init-config \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --server-name updates.example.internal

sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server validate \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --data-root /var/lib/fdupdate-server

sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server install \
  --release-id fdu-017-hawkbit-1.1.0 \
  --install-root /opt/fdupdate-server \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --data-root /var/lib/fdupdate-server
   

 init-config  fails if the destination already exists. It creates random MariaDB
and hawkBit credentials, enables only per-target DDI authentication, disables the
gateway-wide token, anonymous downloads, DMF and Swagger, and creates a private
acceptance PKI. The Compose deployment waits for every health probe. A failed
clean install removes the active link and stops its partial services while keeping
the release directory for diagnosis.

Run the live acceptance path on the same host:

   bash
sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server acceptance \
  --install-root /opt/fdupdate-server \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --data-root /var/lib/fdupdate-server
   

This checks all three running services, verifies the edge certificate, proves that
unauthenticated device/admin/operator requests receive 401, proves that an
operator client certificate reaches the mTLS diagnostic, and confirms that
hawkBit and MariaDB have no published host ports.

   GitHub publisher gateway

Build the gateway locally from the reviewed source, prepare a JSON array of exact
publisher registrations, and install the binary through the deployment CLI:

   bash
cargo build --release --locked -p fdupdate-github-publisher --bin fdupdate-publisher-gateway
sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server install-publisher-gateway \
  --install-root /opt/fdupdate-server \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --data-root /var/lib/fdupdate-server \
  --gateway-binary "$PWD/target/release/fdupdate-publisher-gateway" \
  --registrations-file "$PWD/publisher-registrations.json"
   

The command creates an unprivileged  fdupdate-gateway  service account, generates
the raw 32-byte release-signing seed on the host, copies the private hawkBit
credential into a service-specific root-owned directory, writes the exact runtime
configuration and installs a hardened systemd unit. The service binds only to the
private Docker host-gateway address used by the edge. nginx exposes only the exact
 /v1/publishers/{publisher-id}/releases  route through the trusted HTTPS edge.
Signing material, hawkBit credentials, registrations, request state and audit stay
outside executable releases. The configuration and data roots grant the service
group traverse-only access; its readable and writable permissions stop at the
dedicated publisher configuration, secret and data paths.
Before every service start, a root-only systemd preparation step resolves
hawkBit's current address on the internal Compose network and atomically refreshes
the gateway configuration. Server upgrade and rollback restart the gateway after
container recreation, so no Management API port is published on the host.
The installer sets hawkBit's artifact and multipart limits to 512 MB and 513 MB,
matching the bounded gateway request contract, and recreates hawkBit only when
those settings first change. hawkBit independently enforces a 512 MiB artifact
limit and a 2 GiB tenant artifact-storage quota. Its upload staging tmpfs is
bounded to 768 MB so one maximum-size artifact can be processed without using the
container root filesystem.

The public web runtime serves a stored server-signed release document only at
 /manifests/PROJECT_KEY/RELEASE_ID . It first resolves an exact public repository
publication and verifies the persisted signed payload digest. Private, unknown or
mismatched releases return no document. Signed artifact URLs continue to use the
digest-bound  /downloads/PROJECT_KEY/RELEASE_ID/SHA256  route.

Install or refresh the repository panel after FDUpdater is configured with the
managed  fdupdate-server-host/fdupdate-server/bundle  target. COT must already
serve its authenticated application API on a literal loopback IP. Place the
FDUpdate application credential in a root-owned regular file with mode  0400  or
 0600 ; pass its path, never its value, to the deployment CLI:

   bash
cargo build --release --locked -p fdupdate-web
sudo ./server/deploy/fdupdate-server install-web \
  --install-root /opt/fdupdate-server \
  --config-root /etc/fdupdate-server \
  --data-root /var/lib/fdupdate-server \
  --web-binary "$PWD/target/release/fdupdate-web" \
  --fdupdater-config /etc/fdupdater/FDUpdater.json \
  --cot-service-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8080/ \
  --cot-service-credential-file /etc/cot/fdupdate-service-credential
   

The installer validates the loopback endpoint and exact managed target, then
copies the reader and operator credentials into the root-owned web secret area.
It also validates the COT credential as one bounded visible-ASCII token and
copies it atomically into that protected area.  web.j

title: FDUpdate Server registry
text:
FDUpdate Server registry

 fdupdate-server-registry  owns the product-scoped boundary between signed installation enrollment and private hawkBit target state. Callers provide an authenticated tenant/product  RegistryScope ; the registry never derives scope from client-controlled metadata.

Products and their allowed component IDs are imported idempotently before enrollment. An enrollment request is verified with the installation public key and bound to one instance, tenant, product, component set and nonce. Repeating the exact request returns the existing state. A different key, request or scope for an existing instance fails as a conflict. Reusing one installation public key, nonce or signed request for another instance also fails.

Enrollment remains pending until an authenticated operator explicitly calls  approve ; polling only returns the current signed decision. Approval reconciles a deterministic private hawkBit controller ID and returns the signed client decision defined by  fdupdater-enrollment . Installation credentials are deterministically derived from a separately supplied server credential key, stored only as hashes, and can be rotated. Revocation removes the credential, disables the upstream target, and returns a signed credential-free revoked decision on later polling. Pending, denied, revoked, wrong-product and wrong-tenant access fails closed.

 HawkbitRegistry  is the narrow Management API adapter boundary. Its calls are safe to repeat and registry state changes only after upstream reconciliation succeeds. FDU-021 supplies the authenticated operator API/CLI and audit persistence; FDU-035 supplies the approval panel. Private signing and credential keys must come from a host secret provider and never from repository configuration.

 export_json  emits a bounded credential-free registry snapshot for a transactional durable store, and  from_json  verifies every product, signed enrollment request, fingerprint, state transition invariant and audit sequence before restoring it. The snapshot contains only credential hashes. Using a different credential authority after restore fails closed instead of issuing a replacement credential implicitly.

Approved clients also report product-neutral installed application state through the authenticated application check path. Schema-2 reports bind a canonical request ID, installation, product/component, platform/architecture, local Release/Prerelease channel, installed version, client observation time, server receipt time, optional last successful update, health and a bounded error. Registration, release assignment and reported installation remain separate facts. A publication or assignment never becomes an installed version implicitly.

A managed FDUpdater receives application authority only from an explicit operator binding. The binding names the exact updater instance, product/component, repository, platform, architecture and local channel, and carries separate check and update permissions. Creating or changing a binding uses an expected revision. A stale revision conflicts; disabling a binding advances its revision and immediately denies checks, packages and reports. Repository removal, installation revocation and binding changes are rechecked on every phase, so an older assignment cannot preserve authority. Check-only access may submit authenticated installed-state inventory but receives no release assignment or bytes.

The registry keeps bounded recent per-installation history and projects current state by the newest client observation. Exact retries are idempotent; a reused request ID with different content is a conflict. Delayed offline reports remain in history without replacing newer current state. Successful, failed and rollback outcomes are bound to the authenticated assignment and server-derived repository. Pending, denied, revoked, wrong-instance, wrong-product/component, future-dated and cross-repository reports fail closed. Schema-6 snapshots require the report collection explicitly, schema 7 requires managed-updater heartbeat state, and schema 8 requires the managed-application binding collection. Older snapshots migrate missing collections to an empty state that grants no authority.

Focused verification:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdate-server-registry --locked
cargo clippy -p fdupdate-server-registry --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

title: Server rollout policy
text:
Server rollout policy

 fdupdate-rollout  assigns approved installation IDs to deterministic cumulative waves using a stable salt. Each wave contains only its newly added cohort. The controller advances only after every member reports and the failure rate is at or below the configured threshold.

Missing telemetry, a threshold breach or an operator pause leaves the same wave paused. Resumption is an explicit resolution that clears ambiguous reports and retries that wave; it cannot skip forward. Conflicting duplicate feedback is rejected. FDU-031 adds the mandatory exact-artifact validation-stand promotion gate before this base controller may create a production fleet rollout.

Rollback uses a separate Ed25519 domain and binds the authorization ID, product/component target, exact installed version, exact older destination version, immutable artifact SHA-256 and sequence. The authorization cannot approve another product, component, source version, destination version or artifact. FDUpdater still applies its local signature, compatibility, exact  from_version , artifact-integrity and health rules.

Focused verification:

   text
cargo test -p fdupdate-rollout --test policy --locked
cargo clippy -p fdupdate-rollout --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

title: FDUpdate Server self-update
text:
FDUpdate Server self-update

FDUpdate Server registers as product  fdupdate-server ; database migration, hawkBit and edge components use the same product-neutral FDUpdater target contract as other software. FDUpdater and its bootstrap remain separate host services and outside the server Compose project.

The server adapter downloads and verifies the complete signed release before activation, then persists the update intent and artifact bytes locally. It applies components in the declared dependency order. Each component still passes the ordinary FDUpdater staging, atomic activation and health checks. A rolled-back component stops dependent activation.

Once cached, execution requires no server request. This lets the edge and hawkBit services stop and restart while FDUpdater continues from local state. If candidate health fails, the ordinary transaction engine restores the retained previous slot and restarts it. The result remains local until the server becomes available for reporting.

title: Unified release protocol
text:
Unified release protocol

FDUpdater, embedded application integrations and FDUpdate Server use one signed
release format. The normative wire documents are
 fdupdate/release/v1  and  fdupdate/signed-release/v1 ; their JSON Schemas live in
 crates/fdupdate-contract/schemas .

   Signed authority

The signed manifest binds its monotonically ordered sequence, validity window,
pause state and complete artifact list. Each artifact binds:

- product and component;
- operating-system platform and exact architecture/ABI classifier;
- canonical SemVer version;
- credential-free HTTPS URL, byte size and SHA-256;
- minimum updater and installed/component compatibility;
- rollout cohort and exact-version rollback authorization;
- Ed25519 algorithm, domain, product-scoped key ID and signature.

The manifest signature covers the exact canonical payload bytes. The artifact
signature covers the complete artifact metadata. A transport record, server
release ID, hawkBit action, repository visibility or download credential cannot
replace either signature.

   Platform and ABI

 platform  is  linux  or  windows .  architecture  is an exact bounded canonical
classifier shared by publisher and client. Existing CPU-only values such as
 x86_64  remain valid. Use a stable target classifier such as
 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc  when ABI differences matter. Matching is exact; there is
no alias, normalization or fallback.

   Channels

The locally configured channel applies the same rule in every client and server
resolver:

| Channel | Admitted canonical SemVer |
| --- | --- |
|  release  | Stable versions only; the prerelease component is empty. |
|  prerelease  | Stable and prerelease versions. |

The  prerelease  channel is an opt-in superset so a later stable release remains
eligible. Remote metadata cannot change a target's channel. SemVer build metadata
is rejected because it would permit multiple byte identities behind equal version
precedence.

   Client processing

For every offer, a client:

1. rejects oversized, unknown or noncanonical documents;
2. verifies manifest and artifact signatures using locally trusted product keys;
3. rejects revoked keys, expired releases and replayed sequence/digest pairs;
4. matches exact product, component, platform, architecture/ABI and local channel;
5. checks updater, installed-version and component compatibility, rollout and
   downgrade or rollback authority;
6. downloads within the signed bound and verifies exact size and SHA-256;
7. stages and activates through the local application policy.

Failure before activation preserves the installed application. An executable,
server bundle, SDK archive and application-owned self-update all use this flow.
A statically linked library is replaced only through an update of its owning
application.

   Distribution boundary

FDUpdate Server is the artifact registry. GitHub stores source and may retain
short-lived output from a manually dispatched build, but GitHub Releases are not
used. A manual publication transfers verified bytes to FDUpdate Server, where
public/private discovery and authorized download remain separate from signed
release authority.

The v1 schemas are immutable. A future incompatible field or behavior requires a
new schema identifier, new signature domain where applicable, explicit migration
and compatibility evidence. See  security and trust  security-and-trust.md  and
 software integration  software-integration.md .

title: Validation-stand promotion
text:
Validation-stand promotion

Each product/component policy names exactly one validation installation. A new release or prerelease candidate is initially eligible only for that installation. Missing or multiple assignments reject the rollout.

The stand must report readiness, download, activation, restart and post-update health, then remain healthy through the configured observation period. Completion changes the state to  passed ; it never promotes automatically. A scoped operator creates the immutable promotion record, binding product, component, channel, version, every artifact digest, compatibility digest, stand, evidence digest and operator.

Fleet and canary selection accepts only the exact promoted identity. Changed artifacts, compatibility, channel or target replacement block rollout. Failed or incomplete evidence stays outside all later waves and retains a rollback path. FDUpdater releases use the same gate.
